LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. They need the defense to hold the opponent down entirely, and I'm not sure that even Flores' bunch can do that in the friendly confines of Ford Field. … Prediction: Lions 23, Vikings 14 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) Dajani (Steelers -3.5): How can the Browns keep getting away with this? They overcame a 14-0 deficit in Nashville on Sunday, as Harold Fannin Jr . took a short reception 36 yards down the field with 20 seconds remaining to set up a 32-yard game-winning field goal from Andre Szmyt . Deshaun Watson became the third quarterback since 1970 to register a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of the season. With this being a divisional game against an opponent that just got back from Paris, I can understand why some would take the points with the underdog given the hook. But the Steelers are 3-0 ATS at home. That includes Week 3, when they dropped 30 points on Joe Burrow and the Bengals in a win, and Week 5, when Pittsburgh scored 34 points in a double-digit victory over the Colts. The Steelers are averaging 26.0 points per game over their last five contests, which ranks top 10 in the NFL, and are 8-0 SU and ATS in their last eight home games vs. the Browns. In fact, Pittsburgh is actually a perfect 11-0 ATS in its last 11 home divisional games. Insane stat. … Prediction: Steelers 26, Browns 21 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): I don't understand how the Browns keep doing it. Every single one of their victories has required a game-winning drive in the final five minutes of the game. That's not sustainable on any level whatsoever. The Steelers don't exactly have consistency written all over them, considering the vagaries of their passing game and the fact that their three-game winning streak has come against weak opponents. However, I trust Jaylen Warren and Co. more than I do the Browns at this point. … Prediction: Steelers 20, Browns 13 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) Dajani (Falcons +2.5): I have plenty of questions about both of these teams, but I did tell you the Falcons were going to cover the small number vs. the 49ers last week! Atlanta finished that game on a 26-6 run after trailing 14-3. They scored on four straight drives. I'm not sure the Buccaneers deserve to be three-point favorites this week after that destruction of the Panthers. Baker Mayfield had to throw for just 64 yards and a touchdown in a 43-13 victory, as Bucky Irving , Kenneth Gainwell and Sean Tucker combined for 246 yards rushing and three touchdowns. This Falcons rush defense ranks fourth in the NFL with 88.9 rushing yards allowed per game. Plus, the Falcons have won two road games this season by 20+ points after being listed as an underdog, and are 4-0 ATS in their last four road games against the Buccaneers. … Prediction: Falcons 26, Buccaneers 24 Dubin (Falcons +2.5): The Buccaneers ran all over the Panthers last week, but Atlanta has actually been quite good against the run, allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season. Can Tampa really control the game with Bucky Irving the way it did last week, or will it have to actually turn Baker Mayfield loose as a passer here? If the Bucs have to do that, I have more confidence in Atlanta's offense right now, with Bijan Robinson , Drake London and even Kyle Pitts contributing at a high level. … Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 17 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Dajani ( Broncos +1.5): The Broncos had an embarrassing outing last time they played the Chiefs, allowing 247 yards off of 28 missed tackles in a 31-10 loss. There has been a lot of talk about Bo Nix and the offense, but what about the Chiefs? They averaged 4.3 yards per play and recorded just 213 yards of total offense in that embarrassing loss to the Seahawks. The team seemingly never got off the bus. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 8 picks, including the Bills to top the Ravens in a high-scoring game Imagn Images Going to the dogs last week turned out to be dog doodoo. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going. Pick: Packers 31, Panthers 24 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. It couldn’t possibly go worse than when they lost to the Falcons 35-14 on Thursday night last month. “Yeah, I should change everything, huh?” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon sort-of joked on Wednesday, “because we laid an egg – me I’m talking about. I hold that to ourselves. I think Matt (LaFleur) made some tweaks, which I really liked. I think it’s going to help our guys. We’ll see, the proof will be in the pudding.” The Packers need to find a victory in the pudding against Carolina. Green Bay is in last place in the NFC North and holds a tenuous grip on the final spot in the NFC. Obviously, it’s early to be overly concerned about the playoff race, but the division race is in danger of getting away from them before the calendar flips to November. Will the Packers win? Here are our weekly predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Panthers Prediction The Packers and Panthers are two of the most beat-up teams in the NFL , a fact complicated by playing on a Thursday. The injuries are probably one reason why these also are among the most inconsistent teams in the league. It seems like the Packers have a lot of injuries. But is that true? Here's some good injury data shared by @RotoWire . ⬇️ https://t.co/Mp2IlrCeZW The Packers can’t get out of their own way on offense, which is why they’ve scored 20 or fewer points in four of seven games. They scored only 17 points last week against the Lions, who have one of the worst defenses in the NFL. Detroit entered the game on pace to blow away the dubious league record for passing yards allowed. Jordan Love and Co. failed miserably to capitalize, especially in key moments. The Panthers are no better. Remember Green Bay’s loss to Atlanta at Lambeau? That came just days after Carolina went into Atlanta and won by 31. The Panthers had won three of their last four games until getting steamrolled 43-13 by the Buccaneers. So, which team(s) will show up tonight? So, let’s bring it back to injuries. The Panthers’ starting cornerbacks, Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn, are on injured reserve. Their best pass rusher, Jaelan Phillips, will be inactive due to injury. So, there should be opportunities for the Packers to make plays in the passing game. Combined with a matchup against the worst run defense in the NFL, this could be a breakout game for Green Bay’s offense. “Should be,” of course, is the operative phrase. The only thing the Packers do consistently is play inconsistently. They can’t run the football. They struggle to protect the passer. They drop passes. They misfire on third down and squander opportunities in the red zone. So, should the Packers have a big game offensively? Yes. But will they? At least the defense is good, with Gannon earning his paycheck by fielding a formidable unit that has mostly played winning football even though it can’t rush the passer with a traditional four-man rush. So, who wins? I’d give the advantages to Green Bay on both sides of the ball. On offense, Love should have a strong game against Carolina’s depleted pass defense. Heck, they might even be able to run the football against the league’s worst rush defense. On defense, the Packers have spoken highly of Panthers quarterback Bryce Young all week, but Young is not as good as Detroit’s Jared Goff and the Panthers have only one big-time threat in the passing game compared to two for Detroit. The Panthers will be without their preferred starting offensive tackles, too. So, the Packers will score a key win. A 5-3 start with Micah Parsons still not back on the practice field would be a major victory for a team that has aspirations to be playing deep into January. Bill’s Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 17. Bill’s Record: 5-2. Here are the 10 most important Packers for tonight's game, a story filled with quotes and other good stuff by @JacobWestendorf . ⬇️ https://t.co/tX2pc7MrfW Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Panthers Prediction I don't think this game is going to be pretty. Matt LaFleur said earlier this week that Panthers coordinator Ejiro Evero's defense forces everyone on offense to be consistent on every single play. The Packers have not been like that all season. The injuries on the offensive line make for some uncertainty, and give this coaching staff a chance to screw up the starting five combination, like they have so many times in the past. That being said, Carolina is missing some big guns on defense, including their star pass rusher. Even if Matthew Golden cannot go or is on limited reps, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft should be able to make enough plays in the passing game. Perhaps Josh Jacobs can finally find some room to roam on the ground against the league's worst run defense. Expect a sloppy game, but the Packers will make one more play than the Panthers, getting them to 5-3 before a much-needed mini bye week. Jacob’s Prediction: Packers 17, Panthers 14. away.headline: Green Bay Packers: initial Week 8 injury report release ahead of showdown with Carolina Panthers
away.blurb: The Green Bay Packers were defeated by the Detroit Lions by the score of 20-17 on Sunday afternoon. Despite two missed field goals by rookie Trey Smack and numerous highly questionable penalties called on the defense, the Packers had every opportunity to win the game. As it stands, though, they fell to 4-3 with the loss. Early in the game against Detroit, the Packers lost starting center Sean Rhyan to an ankle injury, and his backup, Jacob Monk, to a quad injury. Earlier today, Monk was placed on injured reserve, and the fear is that Rhyan suffered a high ankle sprain that could keep him out for several weeks. As Green Bay hurries to field a full active roster for Thursday night, they released their initial injury report despite the fact that the team did not practice today. All participation statuses are estimations: As can be seen from the post above, cornerback Benjamin St. Juste was listed as a full participant. This is good news for the Packers secondary, who have been without him for the past several weeks. Aaron Banks, who was active on Sunday, was a limited particpant. home.blurb: He did however take the field for limited participation in Wednesday’s session, and was officially listed as questionable while dealing with foot and shoulder injuries. “Packers WR Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) is listed as QUESTIONABLE for tonight against the Panthers. there is a lot of optimism he’s good to go, Green Bay is expecting him to play I’m told. Green Bay Packers wide receiver Matthew Golden did not participate in practice on Monday or Tuesday as the team prepared for its Week 8 “Thursday Night Football” clash against the Carolina Panthers. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. away.headline: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson expected to play in Week 8: report
away.blurb: Jackson was able to notch limited practice participation leading up to this past Sunday’s Week 7 loss to the Bengals, but he was ultimately ruled out. Now, the Ravens are gearing up for a highly-anticipated Week 8 matchup against the Buffalo Bills. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has missed each of the last three games after suffering an ankle injury in Week 4. The Ravens are 1-2 over that span with Tyler Huntley at the helm, dropping each of their last two games against the division-rival Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals. On Tuesday, NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport confidently reported that Jackson will be on the field for this Week 8 clash. “I expect, based on the people that I’ve spoken with, that Lamar Jackson will play this week. He will be on the field this week against the Buffalo Bills,” Rapoport said. “I know we’ve been here before. This was a 2-3 week injury — he’s through the third week. He is believed to be as close to 100% as he has been and the Ravens do expect him to play.” With Jackson off the field, the Ravens have dropped to last place in the AFC North standings with a 4-3 record. They’ll look to get back in the win column in a difficult road matchup against the Bills this coming Sunday. Sunday’s game will kick off at 1 p.m. ET. The Ravens then have a short week to prepare for a “Thursday Night Football” matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 9. home.headline: Bills injury report: Spencer Brown sits, Tyrell Shavers returns
home.blurb: Brown getting the benefit of a bye week to rest the back injury he assured us was just some soreness and something he tweaked after a long plane ride out west, may not have been enough. Now he is saying he rested through practice in Week 6 so he would be available when the Bills faced the Las Vegas Raiders. He is still sore, still resting – three weeks later. Bills players with limited practice: Moore and Oliver being limited rather than non-participants is encouraging. Sure, it would have been nice to think a week of no football would heal them, but realistically, we may see them on this list all year. So, limited to start the week is a positive. The Buffalo Bills got back to work on Wednesday. The hope has widely been that the bye week would give some added rest to players who had been nursing bumps, bruises, and those injuries that were keeping them from going full speed. While we see one name returning for the first time this season, an extra week of rest may not have been enough for another. _____________________________________________________________________________ OLB Bradley Chubb (chest/thumb) WR Tyrell Shavers – PUP – (knee) There’s plenty of good news in this group. Buffalo opened the 21-day practice window on Shavers. The wide receiver had ACL surgery in late January. He now has until the week before Thanksgiving to get back on the roster. Alford hasn’t healed and Chubb, who noticeably missed some snaps in Week 6, added a chest injury to his list of ailments. The bigger concern is Dalton Kincaid. This is his fourth season in the NFL and we are still looking for a full year of games from him. He did play in 16 his rookie season, but missed four and five the next two years respectively. Bills players with full practice: G Ar’maj Reed-Adams (back/elbow) S C.J. Gardner Johnson (suspended) We can’t be certain that Gardner Johnson’s injury is no longer a problem as he serves a one-week suspension stemming from an on-field altercation in Las Vegas. But an extra week of healing time should help Here’s a look at what the Ravens are dealing with this week. Lamar Jackson is back to practice, as expected. The quarterback has been dealing with a high ankle sprain for the past month causing him to miss the last three games. It looks like he plans to play in Buffalo this weekend.

home.blurb: The Bills come out of their Week 7 bye hoping to get wide receiver D.J. Moore and defensive tackle Ed Oliver back after both missed the previous two games. He did not practice Wednesday or Thursday before the Raiders game but returned on a limited basis Friday and was listed as questionable. Buffalo ultimately kept him inactive. He missed five consecutive practices before returning on a limited basis the Friday before the Raiders game. Oliver was listed as questionable but inactive in Las Vegas. Dalton Kincaid left Buffalo's victory over Las Vegas because of a rib injury but was able to return. The Bills listed him as questionable to return. Kincaid came back in the fourth quarter and caught a 14-yard pass three plays later. Chubb went out during the second quarter and was initially listed as questionable. He returned later in the first half and played 21 of Buffalo's 66 defensive snaps against Las Vegas. T.J. Sanders played against Las Vegas and recorded one tackle after being listed as questionable because of a shoulder injury. His suspension begins Oct. 26 and he can return to Buffalo's active roster Nov. 2, meaning he will miss Sunday's game against Baltimore. Zane Durant is eligible to return after beginning the season on injured reserve. Buffalo can designate Durant to return and open his 21-day practice window when he is medically cleared. Tyrell Shavers is eligible to return after beginning the season on the physically unable to perform list. The Bills can designate him to return and open his 21-day practice window when he is ready. He returned to practice last week and was limited Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. Jackson told reporters Friday that the ankle was improving but that running remained the issue. Baltimore listed Jackson as questionable against the Cincinnati Bengals before ruling him out Saturday. Tyler Huntley started for the third consecutive game and threw for 215 yards in the first half of Sunday's loss. Rookie first-round pick Vega Ioane left the Bengals game near the end of the first quarter because of a knee injury and did not return. Meanwhile, starting right tackle Spencer Brown sat out due to back problems , and seventh-round rookie guard Ar'maj Reed-Adams was a full participant. Seemingly itching to return , Moore had made 91 consecutive regular season appearances before being scratched for the October 12 road contest against the Los Angeles Rams. "The two weeks [out], it was pretty sad. I was mad at myself," said Moore. "Somebody put out a post on X where I was standing there watching the guys practice, that was the hardest thing about the two weeks." Oliver is fighting through a knee injury that happened when he took a hit to the left leg on October 4 against the Patriots. He missed five consecutive practices before returning in a limited capacity on October 16, but was ultimately inactive for the October 18 kickoff in Las Vegas. "There's a reason that Ed Oliver is who Ed Oliver is, and getting him out there and being able to play football again is only going to help our defense and our identity," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady. Right tackle Spencer Brown, tight end Dalton Kincaid and outside linebacker Bradley Chubb, all starters, are new additions on the injury report coming out of the Week 6 game against the Raiders. Additionally, rookie edge rusher TJ Parker, who was on the Week 6 injury report with a rib issue, is now dealing with a knee problem. picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Bengals in Week 8, Why They Won’t, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Heading into Week, the 1-6 Tennessee Titans have everything to prove, but also nothing at all. Especially after last week’s blown two-score lead to the Cleveland Browns, nobody is expecting Robert Saleh’s first team in Nashville to execute a miraculous turnaround. Draft discussions are already becoming relevant, if that tells you anything. Still, the Titans hit the road to face the Cincinnati Bengals this coming Sunday, and it’s a chance for Tennessee to win their second game in three weeks. That’s somehow still an exciting prospect. To preview the matchup, I’ve got one reason the Titans will beat the Bengals, one reason they won’t, and my own prediction for what will actually happen. Let’s start with the former. Will: Titans’ secondary sees massive uptick Two weeks in a row now, Tennessee has forced at least one interception. The Titans have come down with three picks over the last two games, two of which belong to rising offseason pickup Cor’Dale Flott. Tennessee Titans cornerback Cor'dale Flott (18) intercepts Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) on Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. Tennessee is facing one of the best pass-first teams in the NFL. If Saleh's secondary can find consistency beyond the occasional turnover, the Titans would have more than a fair chance to shut down RB Chase Brown on the ground, too. It's much easier to stop Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins in concept than it is on the field, but doing so is the Titans' key to winning this one. Won’t: Titans can't overcome inconsistent Bengals defense The inverse, of course, is if the Titans' offense continues to suffer. The Bengals have proved themselves beatable against "bad" teams - just see their narrow, one-score win over the 1-6 Miami Dolphins two weeks ago. But Cincinnati also just dismantled the Baltimore Ravens last week, 35-13. The through line is that Cincy scored 30+ points in both of those contests; it comes down to the opposing offense's ability to hang in there when Burrow and his crew get hot. Tennessee ranks 31st in both touchdowns and points per game. Almost everywhere the Bengals are in the top 10 through the air, the Titans are in the bottom 10. Cincy has allowed 20+ points in four of their six games this season. If Cam Ward can get back on his feet in any sense of the saying, another 24-point performance like Tennessee had last week could be enough to at least make this one interesting. However, the Titans may need a little more juice than they've seen yet this season from their QB to stay in it. Prediction: Titans lose, 31-20 Ultimately, I have the Titans falling to 1-7 in this one. We've seen a number of trends solidify that this roster has failed to prove their ability to rise beyond. Carnell Tate is the primary receiver in an otherwise underwhelming offense. The defense can force early turnovers, but can't get late stops when it matters - especially when it comes to tackling. Ward has a better second half than his typically abysmal first, but by the time Tennessee tries to get aggressive, it's too late to make a difference. I expect most of, if not all of these notes to be hit in Week 8. I don't think the Titans will lose in a blowout, but on the road against one of the best offenses in the league, this one already looks like too much for Saleh's team. Dybantsa delivers in debut Titans scouting report vs Cincinnati Bengals, matchups, prediction NFL Week 8 Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Positives are hard to find amid the Tennessee Titans' struggles, but running back Tony Pollard was one last week. The Memphis native had his second-best game as a Titans player, with 129 yards rushing and three touchdowns on 25 carries in a gutting 27-24 home loss to the Cleveland Browns on Oct. 25. Maybe Pollard can do it again when the Titans (1-6) face the Cincinnati Bengals (4-2) at Paycor Stadium on Nov. 1 (noon CT, CBS) in NFL Week 8. The Bengals' and Browns ' run defenses are about the same statistically. Cincinnati allows 116.3 rushing yards per game, which ranks 19th in the league. The Titans gained a season-high 322 yards of offense with Pollard's contributions, taking pressure off developing second-year quarterback Cam Ward . (DENNY SIMMONS / THE TENNESSEAN) 1 / 5 Inside Titans vs Browns. Cam Ward, Jeffery Simmons and our best photos Inside Titans vs Browns. Cam Ward, Jeffery Simmons and our best photos More: Now it's Robert Saleh's defense that's letting down the Tennessee Titans | Estes More: Don't blame Cam Ward, Titans offense for blown chances against Cleveland Browns Tennessee coach Robert Saleh pinned the Browns loss on defense . Now that unit will face Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, who's 11th in the league with 1,653 yards passing, and second with 15 passing touchdowns, to go with three interceptions. Here's our scouting report for the Titans' game against the Browns. One Cincinnati Bengals stat to know Cincinnati has 13 pass plays of 25 yards or more this season. Tennessee has seven. Where Tennessee Titans have edge vs. Bengals The good news: Cincinnati's offense ranks 29th in rushing yards per game (81.2), so there's an opportunity for the Titans to make the Bengals one-dimensional. The bad news: Cincinnati's offense is doing fine without a rushing threat, averaging 345.2 yards. It isn't a big Titans advantage, but they must capitalize on it and see if stopping the run allows their pass rush to play like it did against the Colts (six sacks). It will take a stark turnaround after Tennessee allowed a season-high 183 yards rushing against the Browns. That marked the franchise's worst single-game Pro Football Focus run defense grade (36.3) since 2023. Personnel changes up front have not helped. Run-stopping defensive tackle Jordan Elliott was released on Oct. 20 after breaking the NFL's gun policy . Third-year defender Timmy Horne was signed from the practice squad to replace him. Where Cincinnati Bengals have edge vs. Titans Tennessee's secondary tackled poorly and took bad angles against the Browns, making rookie receiver KC Concepcion look like a Pro Bowler (eight catches, 129 yards). Imagine what Burrow and receivers Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase might do. The Titans haven't seen an offense like this in 2026. The Bengals are seventh in the league in passing yards per game (264) and get 76% of their total yards through the air. Higgins and Chase have accounted for nine of the Bengals' 13 explosive pass plays. Saleh's also soul-searching in his secondary. Alontae Taylor was signed in the offseason to fortify one of Tennessee's outside corner spots, but he was made inactive in Week 6 by coach's decision and didn't see the field in Week 7. Now it looks like Taylor will likely move to nickel . This would be a good week for Taylor to make a contribution, assuming Saleh plays him. Score prediction: Bengals 35, Titans 21 The Titans' scarred defense won't be able to slow Burrow, and they can't depend on Ward to keep pace in a shootout. It looks like their worst-case scenario matchup. Winning the turnover battle and making a few plays on special teams would help, but the Titans will be fortunate to keep it within 14 points. He was optimistic after Cincinnati's win over Baltimore that the injury wouldn't be too bad, but it was apparently bad enough to keep him out at least a month. That comes after Tanner Hudson tore a pectoral muscle against the Dolphins. He will miss the rest of the season. That means more targets for Mike Gesicki, who is having his best touchdown season with five scores in six games. As Tennessee continues to key on Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase in the red zone, look for Joe Burrow to keep targeting Gesicki for scoring plays. Tee Higgins goes over 100 yards again Chase has had a slow start to the season, as defenses seem to be keeping him from getting behind them for big plays. He told reporters he thinks he's had opportunities downfield, but the ball just hasn't come his way, and he isn't too concerned. Higgins has been the beneficiary of Chase's slow start and will continue to be. He has had a great season so far, with multiple 100-yard games and no drops through the first seven weeks. Higgins has 90 or more yards in four of his last five games, and he'll extend that stretch against the Titans on Sunday. Joe Burrow gets off to a fast start, throwing two first-half touchdown passes Cincinnati had just six run plays to 13 pass plays in the first half against Baltimore last week, and I think the script will be similar against Tennessee. This time, though, the Bengals will have more success pushing the ball downfield early and will build a two-score lead in the first half. The Tennessee Titans have kept games close, but they've largely faced weaker competition. Expect the Bengals to step on the gas and cover the 10.5-point spread. Cam Ward throws two interceptions Ward has thrown an interception in five straight games heading into Sunday, and Cincinnati's will be one of the best defensive backfields he has faced this season. DJ Turner is playing like an elite cornerback who is about to get paid a lot of money, and Dax Hill is living up to his billing as the complement to Turner that makes the duo so dangerous. Ward will try to force a ball to Carnell Tate, but Turner will intercept it. Then Cincinnati's defensive line will get pressure on Ward, forcing him to rush a throw that Barrett Carter will pick off.

The Cincinnati Bengals are coming off a monster win over the Baltimore Ravens , but they cannot afford to let that lead to them overlooking their next opponent, the Tennessee Titans. I know the Titans are 1-6 and are not a good football team. But this is the NFL, where the margin for error is razor-thin, if that. For the Bengals, this is a prime opportunity to squash any sense of this game being a trap game— coming off a dominant road win at Baltimore and going to Madrid in two weeks— and putting their first complete game together this season. Right now, on FanDuel , the Bengals are a 10.5-point favorite against the Titans. Their moneyline is -650, and the over/under is 46.5 points. This will be Tennessee’s first time playing in Cincinnati since 2020. Ironically, that was Week 8 in 2020 and on November 1st. The Bengals won that game 31-20, which was a coming-out party for Joe Burrow in his rookie season. Burrow was 26/37 for 249 yards and two touchdowns in that game, making a featured appearance on the highlights during NBC’s Sunday Night Football game coverage that night. Since that game, the Bengals and Titans have played four times in Nashville, including in the Divisional round of the 2021 NFL Playoffs. That was the game where Joe Burrow overcame nine sacks and willed the Bengals to a 19-16 win that was the first road playoff win in Bengals history. Cincinnati beat Tennessee 37-27 in Week 15 of the 2024 Season, which was the most recent matchup between the two teams. Tennessee’s head coach is Robert Saleh, in his first season with the Titans. He previously coached the New York Jets and served two stints as the San Francisco 49ers’ defensive coordinator. The Titans are 1-6 and coming off a last-second 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 7. Quarterback Cam Ward is in his second season and has thrown for just 1,179 yards and just four touchdowns this season. Ward also has just one game with over 200 passing yards. Entering Sunday, the Titans were in the bottom two in the NFL in both scoring and total offense, while ranking in the middle of the pack in both scoring and total defense. However, the Titans have been competitive most of the season, as four of their six losses came by one score. Two of them were to the division-leading Giants (12-7) and the aforementioned loss to Cleveland. away.headline: Ja'Marr Chase injury update: Bengals WRs poised to dominate fantasy vs. Titans
away.blurb: Cincinnati is gearing up for a clash against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, but updates earlier in the week raised concerns over Chase’s availability this week. On Thursday, Chase received another update regarding his Week 8 status that alleviated such concerns. Reports indicated Chase’s ankle issue is “not considered to be a major deal”, and the star wideout is expected to suit up this weekend despite a questionable tag. Chase hauled in five of his seven targets during the Week 8 blowout victory, racking up 62 yards with a touchdown, his fifth in the last four games. He enters Sunday’s game ranked as WR16 in PPR leagues, carving out a reliable 16.2 points per week despite some quiet performances and an early bye week. The Bengals have endured some struggles in the run game, and could lean on Burrow and the passing game with expanded volume in Week 8. Despite his ankle issue, Chase should have no problem carving out WR1 fantasy production against the Titans on Sunday, and should be considered a must-start unless he’s officially ruled out. The Cincinnati Bengals are dealing with some injury concerns following a dominant win over the Baltimore Ravens that featured several notable fantasy football performances for Week 7. Star wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase , who eclipsed the 17.0-point mark in PPR for the fourth time in five games, dealt with ankle soreness entering Week 8. Ja’Marr Chase’s Update Bolsters Outlook Against Lowly Titans The Titans present an immensely favorable fantasy matchup for some of the NFL’s biggest stars including Chase, Joe Burrow and Tee Higgins. Tennessee’s defense ranks 24th in the NFL against the pass, and 26th against the run. These marks are likely to fall following the team’s decision to trade Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears on Thursday. Chase’s Injury Could Pave Way For Dominant Tee Higgins Performance Higgins has emerged as the Bengals’ leading receiver through the team’s 4-2 start to the season. He leads Cincinnati’s offense in targets, catches, receiving yards and yards-per-catch, entering Week 8 ranked eighth in receiving with 571 yards along with two touchdowns and 33 catches over 50 targets. Cincy’s WR2 posted his best performance of the season thus far against Baltimore, hauling in six catches for 148 yards and a touchdown, notching a season-high 26.8 PPR points and a WR3 finish in Week 7. Chase’s ankle injury could lead to a greater target share for Higgins once again in Week 8, potentially creating additional red zone targets for the star receiver. Considering the momentum Higgins is riding into Week 8, he should be in for another team-high receiving performance this week as Chase continues to nurse soreness in his ankle. The Cincinnati Bengals are dealing with some injury concerns following a dominant win over the Baltimore Ravens that featured several notable fantasy football performances for Week 7. Star wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase , who eclipsed the 17.0-point mark in PPR for the fourth time in five games, dealt with ankle soreness entering Week 8. Ja’Marr Chase’s Update Bolsters Outlook Against Lowly Titans The Titans present an immensely favorable fantasy matchup for some of the NFL’s biggest stars including Chase, Joe Burrow and Tee Higgins. Tennessee’s defense ranks 24th in the NFL against the pass, and 26th against the run. These marks are likely to fall following the team’s decision to trade Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears on Thursday. Chase’s Injury Could Pave Way For Dominant Tee Higgins Performance Higgins has emerged as the Bengals’ leading receiver through the team’s 4-2 start to the season. He leads Cincinnati’s offense in targets, catches, receiving yards and yards-per-catch, entering Week 8 ranked eighth in receiving with 571 yards along with two touchdowns and 33 catches over 50 targets. Cincy’s WR2 posted his best performance of the season thus far against Baltimore, hauling in six catches for 148 yards and a touchdown, notching a season-high 26.8 PPR points and a WR3 finish in Week 7. Chase’s ankle injury could lead to a greater target share for Higgins once again in Week 8, potentially creating additional red zone targets for the star receiver. Considering the momentum Higgins is riding into Week 8, he should be in for another team-high receiving performance this week as Chase continues to nurse soreness in his ankle. Tennessee Titans rookie and leading receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder) did not practice on Oct. 28, according to the team's injury report. DL John Franklin-Myers (Groin), DNP WR Calvin Ridley (Hip), Limited WR Carnell Tate (Shoulder), DNP P Tommy Townsend (Left Knee), DNP Punter Tommy Townsend also missed practice with a knee injury, prompting the team to sign Thomas Morstead. Tate has a team-high 34 catches for 413 yards and a touchdown this season. Tennessee (1-6) plays the Cincinnati Bengals (4-2) at Paycor Stadium on Nov. 1 (noon CT, CBS). Titans punter Tommy Townsend (knee) also didn't practice after sustaining a first-half injury against the Cleveland Browns and missing the rest of the game. Tennessee signed punter Thomas Morstead to the practice squad on Oct. 28. "Tommy is still hurting from the game," Saleh said before practice. "We're not sure. We're still working through the week to see if he can make it. We signed a punter just in case. We'll know more by the end of the week." Townsend is averaging 49.2 yards on 30 punts through seven games. Saleh knows the 40-year-old Morstead, a fifth-round draft pick of the New Orleans Saints in 2009. Morstead played for the Saints (2019-2020), New York Jets (2021, 2023-24), Atlanta Falcons (2021), Miami Dolphins (2022), and San Francisco 49ers (2025). He was on the Indianapolis Colts practice squad earlier in the 2026 season. Saleh was the Jets coach during Morstead's time there and the defensive coordinator at San Francisco when Morstead played for the 49ers. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Cowboys (3-4) take the field Sunday at AT&T Stadium against the Cardinals (2-5) looking to build on the momentum from their win Monday Night over the Eagles. Dallas sits second in the NFC East, one and a half games behind the Giants. Arizona sits in the cellar in the NFC West already four games behind the 49ers. Dallas’ win 38-21 Monday night was its most encouraging performance of the season. Dak Prescott threw for 212 yards and three touchdowns without an interception, including two scores to CeeDee Lamb , as the Cowboys erased a 21-20 third-quarter deficit and scored the final 18 points. We buried the headline, however. Javonte Williams rushed for a career-high 155 yards and a touchdown, helping Dallas pile up 204 rushing yards. Arizona’s latest loss illustrated one of its biggest problems. The Cardinals produced 353 yards and controlled the ball for more than 33 minutes against Denver, but went just 1-for-5 in the red zone in the 30-16 defeat. Quarterback Jacoby Brissett completed 27 of 48 passes for 272 yards and a touchdown, with Trey McBride catching 10 passes for 111 yards and the score. Offensively, Dallas has been considerably more productive, averaging 27.0 points and 353.6 yards per game, compared with Arizona’s 20.3 points and 313.9 yards. The Cardinals do own the better turnover differential at plus-2, compared with minus-3 for Dallas, giving Arizona one potential route to an upset Sunday. Dallas’ biggest storyline Sunday is whether the Prescott-Lamb passing game and Williams-led rushing attack can sustain the balance they finally showed against Philadelphia. The Cardinals have been one of the best teams at winning the time of possession battle but one of the worst in the red zone. They must find a way to turn their long drives into touchdowns. Recent history is important here, particularly because Arizona has repeatedly caused Dallas problems of late. The Cowboys lead the all-time series 56-36-1, but Arizona has won four straight regular-season meetings. Arizona won 27-17 in their most recent meeting against Dallas on November 3, 2025. That last meeting has particular relevance because Brissett and Prescott were also the quarterbacks: Brissett, starting with Kyler Murray sidelined, went 21-of-31 for 261 yards and two touchdowns and also ran for a score, while Prescott threw for 250 yards with one touchdown and an interception and was sacked five times. Arizona committed no turnovers, Dallas committed three, and the Cardinals converted three of four red-zone possessions into touchdowns. Let’s dive into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. away.headline: Cowboys defenders Quinnen Williams, Caleb Downs added to injury report vs. Cardinals
away.blurb: Rookie defensive back Caleb Downs was limited in a walkthrough practice with an ankle injury. Defensive tackle Quinnen Williams was also a new addition to the injury report as he's dealing with a hamstring injury. He was limited on Wednesday. FRISCO - The Cowboys added some new names to the injury report Wednesday. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Tuesday that there were a few players dealing with some minor injuries, but nothing significant. The Cowboys could also be on the verge of some players returning . Safety PJ Locke III (foot) and outside linebacker Marist Liufau (forearm) were both full participants Wednesday. Locke was added to injured reserve after hurting his foot in the Week 2 win over the Washington Commanders. Liufau fractured his forearm in the preseason finale. The Cowboys created one roster spot earlier this week when they waived running back Emari Demercado. He was claimed by the Houston Texans on Wednesday. If the Cowboys activate both Locke and Liufau, they'll have to make one more roster move. Cowboys safety Jalen Thompson, another player on injured reserve , was seen working in the rehabilitation group during practice. He's been on injured reserve since he suffered a hamstring injury in late September. His practice window hasn't been opened yet. Read this story on dallasnews.com

home.headline: Dallas Cowboys on brink of getting more reinforcements back on defense
home.blurb: Cowboys DT Jonathan Bullard Nearing Return From Injury The Cowboys announced Thursday that they have opened up the 21-day practice window for defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard, who had been on injured reserve for the past four games after suffering a calf injury in Week 3's loss to the Baltimore Ravens. If he doesn't return during that window, Bullard will be placed on season-ending injured reserve. Either way, Bullard eventual return might get overlooked but it will bring some much-needed depth back to the defensive line. What Jonathan Bullard's Potential Return Can Do for Dallas Bullard's return will allow players like Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark to rotate out knowing that a veteran with over 130 games of regular-season experience is stepping in for them. Fans will have to wait and see what that looks like on a week-to-week basis once Bullard makes his potential return. Cowboys Get Much-Needed Secondary Reinforcements With Safety Return The Dallas Cowboys were hit with major injury issues early this season, particularly on the defensive side of the ball. Each week following the season opener, it seemed like a starter or key rotational piece was going down with injury, and this certainly didn't help a defense that was already having its struggles under first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker. But in Week 7's win over the Philadelphia Eagles, the Cowboys welcomed back linebacker DeMarvion Overshown and cornerback Cobie Durant to the lineup after multi-week absences due to respective hamstring injuries. Now, it's looking like the Cowboys could soon be getting back a notable member of their defensive line as the midway point of the season arrives. It remains to be seen if Bullard will be ready in time for Sunday's home game against the Arizona Cardinals, though it feels like a more realistic target date could be Week 9 at the Indianapolis Colts. During the first three games with Dallas this year, Bullard has just three total tackles and two quarterback hits but he has a decade of NFL experience that fans have yet to see on display this season. After signing with the Cowboys this offseason following one year with the New Orleans Saints, Bullard admitted that Dallas' defense fits what he's used to. "I think the defense they're trying to bring in is what I've done for the last 10 years," Bullard said. "To come in and be a big end, and be present on run downs, to make it tougher for teams to run the ball — for us to get the run defense going. To have the opportunity to come here, it just fit." The Vikings, which have yet to lose a game this season (6-0), feature both a bottom-10 offense (20.8 points/game) and the league's top defensive unit. Coordinated by Brian Flores, Minnesota's defense has permitted just 12.3 points a game, and hasn't allowed more than 16 points in a game since Week 2. And most recently, the Vikings surrendered just 10 points in a 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7. Additionally, Minnesota has been extremely stout against the pass thus far this season. In fact, Kevin O'Connell's squad has allowed the second-fewest passing yards (930) and the least amount of touchdowns through the air (three) through the season's first seven weeks. The Vikings have also already secured seven interceptions, spearheaded by cornerback Byron Murphy's league-high three picks. So, Lions signal-caller Jared Goff, who has yet to throw an interception in 2026, will face arguably his biggest test of the campaign against Minnesota's stingy pass defense . Then on the opposite side of the ball, Detroit's secondary will receive one of its toughest assignments of the year, going head-to-head with All-Pro wideout Justin Jefferson. Jefferson, who has surpassed 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first six NFL seasons, has accumulated 302 reception yards and three touchdowns in five games this season. He's unquestionably Vikings passer Kyler Murray's go-to target and one of the very best receivers in the game today. Subsequently, D.J. Reed, the Lions’ No. 1 cornerback , should get the majority of one-on-one reps with the Pro Bowl pass-catcher. Additionally, I wouldn't be surprised if Detroit defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard deployed a rotation of corners in the Week 8 tilt. And as a result, I could see the likes of Ennis Rakestraw and Roger McCreary also getting opportunities to defend Jefferson Sunday. It'll hardly be an easy task for the Lions’ defensive backs group. However, Detroit does have a solid track record against Jefferson, having limited him to under 60 yards the past three meetings between the NFC North rivals . And if the Lions could do it a fourth straight time, it would go a long way toward Dan Campbell's squad notching its fifth victory on the season. At this present juncture, I'm willing to give Detroit a 61 percent chance to secure the Week 8 victory . picks.headline: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions as Heading Into NFC North Collision vs. Lions in Week 8
picks.blurb: Just like that, the November gauntlet is here. Your 6-0 Vikings head to Detroit this weekend to battle the 4-2 Lions for the first time since their Christmas matchup last season. With an undefeated record and divisional seeding on the line, the stakes are certainly high. Will this be the week that finally proves the Vikings are worthy of their record ? Will Kyler Murray and the offense finally get on track? Will the defense finally meet their match? Let’s dive into my predictions for Sunday’s massive matchup. 1. Justin Jefferson hits for 100 receiving yards This may come as a shock, but Justin Jefferson has had only one 100-yard receiving game since Oct. 5, 2025 . With the Vikings’ passing game desperate for a spark against a weak Lions pass defense, Sunday may be the perfect chance to stack some yardage. Detroit’s defensive back group is shaky, to say the least. The Lions currently allow the most passing yards per game in the NFL, averaging a whopping 291.8. The return of safety Brian Branch last week against the Packers certainly helps their case, especially if fellow safety Kerby Joseph is close behind after being cleared to return to practice. But their cornerback group should give Jefferson plenty of opportunities to gain yardage this weekend. Ennis Rakestraw Jr. was listed as limited in practice on Wednesday , placing even more pressure on D.J. Reed. 2. NFC North rivals combine for seven or more sacks Even though the Lions give up a ton of yardage on defense, their pass rush is not to be ignored. They’re tied with the Vikings, Bengals, Broncos, and Texans for a league-leading 21 sacks. Basically, Sunday could be a bad day to be a quarterback at Ford Field. Star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson and former Viking D.J. Wonnum each have five sacks for the Lions so far, while rising Vikings star Dallas Turner is tied for the third-most sacks in the league with six. I predict both defensive fronts will continue to cause chaos on Sunday, and that there will be at least seven total sacks between both teams. With the Vikings’ inconsistent interior offensive line , Kyler Murray will need to be ready to take off to keep that number from getting even higher. 3. The Vikings lose the battle but win the war There is a case to be made that a loss on Sunday would be the best thing for the Vikings with less than two weeks left before the trade deadline . Obviously, you’d love to win every game, but the lessons learned from a loss may actually set this squad up for better long-term success. The Vikings’ defense has been stellar, but the Lions' high-flying offense presents the hardest challenge they’ve faced this year. Can the offense be trusted in its current state to step up and score points? If not, the Vikings will likely suffer their first loss of the year and hopefully walk away with valuable lessons from the experience. If it motivates general manager Nolan Teasley to make a splash deal at the deadline , it may prove to be a good outcome in the long run. Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Kole Noble, Mike Payton, Tyler Forness, Wendell Ferreira Thu, October 29, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings are undefeated with an elite defense, but this is their first big test with the Detroit Lions. In Week 7, the Minnesota Vikings will be facing their third NFC North opponent of the season, and second on the road when they face the Detroit Lions on Sunday afternoon. The game is a battle between two of the best units in the NFL, with Brian Flores' defense trending at a historic pace against a Lions offense that has consistently made things difficult on the Vikings. Jared Goff has been the key to that success, finding ways to attack Flores' blitz heavy scheme. Even with that success, it didn't resonate last season, as the Vikings won both games. Will that trend continue? Our experts predicted the pivotal NFC North game. Vikings 16, Lions 10 We can talk about how this matchup is one of the bigger ones across the league, especially this week with both teams with a winning record, but the one matchup that has me curious is Flores vs. Goff. We've seen a really interesting split with how much success Goff has had at quarterback against Flores. Goff with Ben Johnson: 4-0 Goff without Johnson: 0-2 Johnson without Goff: 1-2 Are we sure that the combination of Goff and Johnson was the secret sauce together and not just one of them? With how Flores has evolved the defense, the short routes over the middle of the field aren't there the way they used to, and that will be the difference. – Tyler Forness , A to Z Minnesota (2-2 record) Vikings 20, Bears 14 The Minnesota Vikings have been winning games with a clear formula the last few weeks and that formula has been dominating teams on defense. Until a team actually finds a way to get the better of Brian Flores' unit, I'm going to side with Minnesota. Detroit certainly has a lot of firepower on offense to score a ton of points, but Flores held this offense to 10 and 24 points in their last two matchups. In those last two games, quarterback Jared Goff was sacked 5 times in each game. We all know that if you get pressure on Goff up the middle, he's going to struggle. Minnesota has been pressuring the quarterback better than anyone this season. I see the Vikings scoring just enough points to secure a seventh straight win while Flores puts Goff in a blender yet again. – Kole Noble , A to Z Chicago (0-4 record) Lions 23, Vikings 17 This is a wild matchup because, by EPA/play, the Lions are third on offense and 32nd on defense, while the Vikings are first on defense and 30th on offense. So it's a two-headed matchup with strength versus strength and weakness versus weakness. However, my inclination is to think the Lions have a slight advantage despite the challenges of facing a Brian Flores' defense. Since Flores took over as the Vikings defensive coordinator in 2023, the Lions have averaged 26 points a game versus Minnesota. Outside of the second game last year, when the Lions scored 10, it's been consistently good. Jared Goff has been protected, the communication along the offensive line has been excellent, and that's how you make Goff play at his highest level. The Lions' secondary is bad, but it certainly got better with Brian Branch getting back. And up front, it's been mostly a viable performance. So, I'm going with Detroit in this one. – Wendell Ferreira , A to Z Green Bay (1-3 record) Lions 17, Vikigns 14 Ultimately, it's going to come down to who can score in this game, and while the Vikings' defense is on the verge of being historically good, the Lions' offense is arguably the best in the league right now, and they get this game at home. It's not going to be easy. It should be a back-and-forth affair all day long, and it should be an ugly one. But I have the Lions winning 17-14 and ending the Vikings' undefeated streak. – Mike Payton , A to Z Detroit (2-2 record) Final Prediction for Vikings vs. Bears Last week, our NFC North beat writers were split on the Vikings against the Green Bay Packers, and this week is no different. It's a fascinating matchup, and the curious element will be the Bears' offense. Are they who we think they are, or a flash in the pan like the 2024 New Orleans Saints with Klint Kubiak? From a fantasy football standpoint, this divisional clash presents a fascinating dilemma: Detroit boasts one of the league's most explosive scoring offenses , but Brian Flores' Vikings defense has been the stingiest unit in football, holding opponents to league-low numbers on third downs and in the red zone. Here is how you should manage your key Detroit Lions skill players in fantasy lineups this week. Amon-Ra St. Brown (WR) *Verdict: Mandatory Start (WR1) *The Breakdown: Never overthink your elite talent. Amon-Ra St. Brown remains Jared Goff's undisputed safety valve, commanding a massive target share regardless of game script. While Minnesota's defense excels at limiting big plays downfield, they rely heavily on blitzing to disrupt timing. That operates directly into St. Brown's favor. He thrives on quick-slants, intermediate crossers, and screen setups designed to beat the blitz. Expect heavy volume and a high PPR floor with strong touchdown potential in a high-leverage home game. Jahmyr Gibbs (RB) *Verdict: High-End RB1 Start *The Breakdown: Jahmyr Gibbs is a matchup-proof fantasy asset due to his explosive dual-threat ability out of the backfield. Minnesota's aggressive pass rush often forces opposing quarterbacks to dump the ball off quickly—an area where Gibbs excels. Even if rushing lanes inside are tight against a disciplined Minnesota front seven, Gibbs' involvement in the short passing game gives him a massive ceiling in PPR formats. Lock him into your starting running back slot. Jared Goff (QB) *Verdict: Sit in 1QB Leagues / Low-End Superflex Option * The Breakdown: Goff has been remarkable this season, operating with zero interceptions and elite efficiency. However, Minnesota's defense presents his absolute worst fantasy matchup to date. Brian Flores leads a pass rush tied for the league lead in sacks, generating persistent pressure without sacrificing coverage behind it. Historically, Goff's fantasy output takes a hit when forced off his spot and out of rhythm. Detroit will likely lean on the ground game and methodical short passes, capping Goff's passing yardage and touchdown upside. Look for a safer QB1 alternative if available. Jameson Williams (WR) *Verdict: Risky Flex / Bench Option *The Breakdown: Jameson Williams is the ultimate home-run hitter, but this is a dangerous week to rely on deep shots. Minnesota's primary defensive objective is keeping plays in front of them and preventing explosive vertical completions. Combined with expected edge pressure that limits the time needed for deep routes to develop, Williams carries a dangerously low floor this week. Unless you are chasing high variance in a matchup where you are a heavy underdog, keep "Jamo" on the bench. Sam LaPorta (TE) *Verdict: TE1 Start (Based on position scarcity) *The Breakdown: Tight end remains a thin position across fantasy football, keeping Sam LaPorta in line for starting lineups. However, temper your expectations for a blow-up game. Minnesota has limited tight end production over their six-game winning streak. LaPorta should see targets as a blitz-beater alongside St. Brown, making him a fine start, but expect more of a steady PPR floor than a slate-winning performance.

picks.headline: Vikings at Lions: Predictions, picks and odds for NFL Week 8 game
picks.blurb: 1. Defense wins championships, but will it win this game? The Lions and Vikings couldn't be more opposite at this point in the season. Minnesota is winning with defense, and Detroit is getting by with an electric offense. So it'll be strength vs. strength and weakness vs. weakness in this key NFC North clash. 2. Not-so smooth sailing: The Vikings are about to enter some rough waters when the calendar flips to November. Minnesota cleaned up with wins over the Saints , Dolphins and Colts in October, but the schedule's difficulty is about to be turned up a notch. The Lions, Bills, Packers and Niners await in the penultimate month of the year for the last undefeated team. We're about to find out if the Vikings are a contender or pretender. 3. Scoring drought: For the first time this season, Jahmyr Gibbs didn't get into the end zone. For someone who has his eyes on LaDainian Tomlinson's record of 31, that drought can't last much longer. Gibbs has nine total touchdowns through six games, but he'll still have to pick up the pace. That watch continues into Week 8. That travels. But the Lions present a much tougher offensive assignment than the Colts, especially with Jahmyr Gibbs creating problems as both a runner and receiver. Detroit's best approach is keeping Jared Goff out of obvious passing situations, where Brian Flores can turn an ordinary Sunday into an escape room. Minnesota's historically bad offense remains the concern. Can it consistently hold up its end against a team capable of sustaining drives? I'm expecting a tight, physical division game, with the Lions bouncing back to produce just enough offense to hand the Vikings their first loss. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Lions 20, Vikings 13 This might be the end of the line for the Vikings' undefeated run. While Brian Flores' vise-grip defense gives Minnesota a chance in any contest, it will be exceedingly difficult if the Kyler Murray-led offense remains out of sync. Deroit's defense isn't inspiring fear in anyone, but Brian Branch's return has helped the unit at least approach reliability. Jared Goff has the third-highest passer rating of any quarterback against the blitz this year, so Flores might have to be particularly creative in how he tries to box in the Lions' attack. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Lions 21, Vikings 17 Unstoppable force meets immovable object. The Lions defense couldn't catch a cold this season, and the Vikings offense appears to be doing their best to boost Brian Flores' chances of landing a head coaching job this offseason. If you like chaos, this Flores defense is for you. Physical and blitz-heavy, Minnesota is the last unbeaten team solely because of that unit. However, it's hard to have any faith in the Kyler Murray-led unit on the other side of the ball. This figures to be an ugly NFC North contest. Trust the Lions' offense to eke out a win at home. away.headline: Vikings get positive injury update on RB Aaron Jones: report
away.blurb: The veteran ball carrier exited the game in the fourth quarter as the Vikings posted 10 unanswered points to secure a 16-10 win over the visiting Colts. He was listed as questionable to return, but did not. Minnesota Vikings running back Aaron Jones left Sunday’s win over the Indianapolis Colts with a knee injury. Fortunately for the Vikings, this injury for Jones doesn’t appear to be serious. On Monday, ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter reported a positive update on the Vikings RB. “Vikings RB Aaron Jones’ knee injury that he suffered during Sunday’s win over the Colts is not considered to be significant at this time, and a source described him as ‘day to day,'” Schefter reported. This injury for Jones occurred in the same game that fellow running back Jordan Mason returned from injured reserve. Mason missed each of the Vikings’ last four games after suffering a thumb injury in Week 1, forcing Jones to step up as the team’s bell-cow lead back. Mason led the Vikings in rushing on Sunday, taking 15 carries for 68 yards. Jones recording 26 yards on eight carries before exiting the game. The Vikings are the NFL’s last remaining undefeated team, boasting a 6-0 recording heading into this coming Sunday’s Week 8 matchup against the Detroit Lions. home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Lions, Kerby Joseph had his 3-week window to return from the PUP list opened this week, but he is unlikely to play on Sunday. Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown did not practice Wednesday with shoulder and ankle injuries, respectively, which is something to keep an eye on the rest of the week. For the Vikings, Kevin O'Connell didn't seem overly concerned about either Aaron Jones or Joe Huber. Jones is considered day-to-day while Huber sitting out practice on Wednesday was more precautionary than a sign he won't play on Sunday. Brian O'Neill continues to play through a minor knee injury. We'll see how it plays out with injury updates tomorrow and Friday. picks.blurb: 1. Klint Kubiak vowed there was "no controversy" at quarterback, where Kirk Cousins will remain the starter. While the 38-year-old might have hit a wall last week in trying to navigate the Rams ' relentless blitzes, the NFL's leading passer is hardly the Silver and Black's biggest problem. Kubiak has bemoaned an inert running game that has left Las Vegas needing to sling its way back into games. It could be tricky to get things going against a Jets defense that ranks fifth in defensive EPA per rush. 2. Can New York finally get Garrett Wilson involved early and often in the offensive game plan? One week after he was essentially a non-factor against the Patriots, Wilson was held without a reception or target in the first half against a woefully undermanned Dolphins secondary. Wilson and Glenn both downplayed the wideout's heated confrontation with quarterback Geno Smith, but expect feeding the receiver early and often to be a point of emphasis for Gang Green. 3. How the Raiders' defense handles the Jets' ground game could determine the course of the game. The Silver and Black allowed a season-high 199 rushing yards to the Rams last week, with a vulnerability that has been apparent all season finally reaching critical mass. New York, meanwhile, has seen Braelon Allen eclipse 100 rushing yards in two of the last three games he's handled as Breece Hall's fill-in. Geno Smith gets his former team, while Kirk Cousins keeps the Raiders' starting job despite the growing curiosity about Fernando Mendoza. Neither team has earned much trust lately, so let's acknowledge that before pretending this is an easy handicap. Smith threw three touchdowns against Miami, and Las Vegas' defense offers an opportunity for another productive afternoon. The Raiders need more from their running game to keep Cousins from carrying every possession. I'm giving New York the slightest edge at the Meadowlands, and a fifth straight loss for Las Vegas. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Jets 24, Raiders 20 This game could end up shaping the second half of the season for two coaching staffs that seem to be at a crossroads. The Jets' secondary might not be able to mug the Raiders' receiving corps the way that the Patriots and Rams did, but the pass rush should be able to generate sufficient heat to keep Kirk Cousins out of sorts. Las Vegas seems desperate to find any semblance of offensive balance - as well as some stops against the run - but a breakthrough might not materialize this week. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Raiders 26, Jets 20 You can put a bow on the 2026 Jets. The season, and maybe the Aaron Glenn era, came to an end with a loss to the Dolphins in Week 7. It's going to be a bumpy ride to the finish, but there is no doubt the destination is a top pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. That's why it's fitting that New York will get a glimpse at what it could've had last season. Fernando Mendoza won't play, but it's the idea he's wearing silver and black that sticks. The Raiders are just better. Vegas gets back on track.
