Tonka Hemingway and Quay Walker participated in practice on a limited basis on Thursday. When asked if running back Mike Washington earned more reps, Kubiak stated, "Yes," he had. Washington was listed on the injury report as a limited participant on Wednesday and did not practice on Thursday afternoon. This could be bad news for the Raiders. Or it could be precautionary, since Bowers missed Friday's practice before his first start of the season, and Jeanty did not practice late in Week 5 before Las Vegas faced the New England Patriots, but he still played that Sunday . Washington averaged about five carries per game before last Sunday. Heading into Week 6, Jeanty averaged nearly 18 carries per game before that number was cut in half last Sunday, as Washington carried the ball double his season average per game. If Washington is out on Sunday against the Rams , Jeanty's health and durability will be tested. home.headline: New York Jets Add David Bailey, Braelon Allen to Injury Report
home.blurb: The latest addition is star rookie edge rusher David Bailey, who has a groin injury that is keeping him out of practice on Wednesday. Bailey sustained the injury against the Dolphins, but finished the game. Head coach Aaron Glenn said Bailey came to the Jets practice facility on Monday and said his groin injury was still bothering him. Glenn declined to speculate on whether the injury would keep Bailey out of the game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. "We'll see how he operates," the coach said. "We'll see during the week." Bailey did not practice on Wednesday, with Glenn waiting until later in the week to make an official game status designation. Of greater concern may be the absence of defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat. The biggest player in the NFL, Sweat sustained a knee injury against the Dolphins and is listed as doubtful. Also doubtful for the Raiders game is edge Joseph Ossai, who has an ankle injury. Both are considered week-to-week on availability. Also nursing an ankle is running back Braelon Allen, who ran for more than 100 yards against the Dolphins. He was listed as limited for Wednesday's practice. The Jets' other star running back, Breece Hall, may return against the Raiders after being a game-time no-go against the Dolphins. He has 357 yards since Hall went down in Week 3, and has performed so well that the Jets are trying to scheme a way to have both backs on the field at the same time. He returned to practice this week and has been limited in drills Wednesday and Thursday before Friday’s session. Taylor, at least, was seen participating in team stretch and then running and cutting on the side of practice, but he was still deemed a non-participant in practice. Rookie safety Kyle Louis, as he returned to practice this week, appears to be a Saturday decision on whether he is activated off injured reserve with the knee issue suffered in the opener against the Raiders. Listed as questionable, he is at least in play to return. For the Jets, coach Aaron Glenn told reporters Friday running back Breece Hall will be questionable, which held true at the release of the injury report. Hafley said he expects Hall to play after the standout rusher missed three games and he's preparing as such. New York has linebacker and Miami Hurricanes alum Kiko Mauigoa (quadriceps), offensive lineman Max Mitchell (concussion), edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle) ruled out. Before Friday’s practice, Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Douglas will be good to go after missing three games with an ankle injury. The team’s injury report listed Douglas free of any game status designation after he underwent a full practice session. On Friday, Douglas appeared to be moving well running routes on air and catching passes from quarterback Malik Willis . “He's made a bunch of plays in practice,” said Hafley, who noted Douglas had taken part in individual and team portions of practice before Friday. “I'm excited to see him play. He hadn't played in a while. … It brings us some extra juice.” Without him, the Miami passing offense ranks 31st among 32 teams in the league on the year. Courtesy of Wednesday's practice report , defensive back Doneiko Slaughter was listed as a non-participant with a hamstring injury. Slaughter was not listed on the Week 7 practice report, and it is not known when he picked up this new hamstring injury. Slaughter, who played collegiate football at Tennessee (2020–2023) and Arkansas (2024), began his NFL career as an undrafted free agent with the Jacksonville Jaguars . Slaughter would later sign a reserve/future contract with the Steelers in January 2026. He was unfortunately released during final roster cuts but subsequently signed with the Steelers' practice squad. Slaughter was elevated from the practice squad for the Steelers' first three games of the season and was signed to the active roster on October 1. He was later waived but ultimately brought back on October 10, where he now remains a vital depth contributor on the 53-man roster. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton No one predicted the Browns (5-2) would be tied for first in the AFC North heading into Week 8 of the NFL season, but here they sit as they prepare to play the Steelers (5-2) in Pittsburgh this Sunday. Cleveland has won five of its last six after beating Tennessee 27-24 last Sunday, while Pittsburgh enters on a three-game winning streak following a 16-10 victory over New Orleans in the NFL’s first regular-season game in Paris. The matchup also comes only a month after Cleveland beat Pittsburgh 27-24 on October 1. Last week, Cleveland again showed an ability to win late in their game against Tennessee. After falling behind 14-0 in the first quarter, the Browns rallied behind Quinshon Judkins , who rushed for 96 yards and two touchdowns, and rookie KC Concepcion , who caught eight passes for 129 yards. Deshaun Watson delivered perhaps his best performance of the season, completing 25 of 36 passes for 308 yards while adding a nine-yard rushing touchdown. After Tennessee tied the game with 58 seconds remaining, Watson immediately answered, hitting Harold Fannin Jr. for 36 yards to help set up Andre Szmyt’s game-winning 32-yard field goal as time expired. It was Watson’s fifth fourth-quarter winning drive of the season. Pittsburgh’s latest win was less dramatic but built around the combination it hopes can carry them to a division title and a playoff berth: Aaron Rodgers , an effective running game and a defense capable of closing out tight games. Rodgers completed 19 of 30 passes for 212 yards and a touchdown against New Orleans, including a four-yard score to Darnell Washington that gave him 540 career touchdown passes and moved him past Peyton Manning into third place in NFL history. Jaylen Warren supplied 101 rushing yards on 18 carries. The Pittsburgh defense held the Saints to just 18 rushing yards and Payton Wilson produced a red-zone interception. The biggest storyline may simply be whether Pittsburgh can reverse what happened in Cleveland four weeks earlier. In that Oct. 1 meeting, the Browns built a 21-7 advantage before Rodgers led a fourth-quarter comeback, eventually tying the game at 24 on his three-yard touchdown pass to Pat Freiermuth and ensuing two-point run. Watson then went 4-for-5 for 46 yards on Cleveland’s final drive, positioning Szmyt for a 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds remaining to give the Browns a 27-24 victory. Watson finished with 268 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Rodgers threw for 299 yards and three touchdowns but was intercepted twice; DK Metcalf added 115 receiving yards and Warren ran for 93. That first meeting established the template for Sunday: division rivals comfortable playing close games led by veteran quarterbacks who have repeatedly delivered late, and a Browns team trying to complete an improbable season sweep against a Steelers club returning home looking to reclaim the upper hand in the AFC North. Let’s dive into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. away.blurb: The first injury report of the week sets the tone for what comes next. Some names are expected after a physical game, while others appear out of nowhere and change how a team prepares. With a division title race heating up, every name matters. The Browns’ first report ahead of their trip to Pittsburgh included a few new concerns. The biggest surprise is Verse. He did not practice because of a knee injury, a new issue for one of Cleveland’s most important defenders. Verse has not recorded a sack since arriving in the Myles Garrett trade, but the extra blockers he draws have been a big part of the Browns’ pass rush. He also made headlines after the first meeting with Pittsburgh when he called out the Steelers’ protection and said he could not wait to see them again. Howard is another new concern. The starting right tackle did not practice and is in the concussion protocol, which means he must clear several steps before he can play Sunday. Jenkins also sat out with a knee injury. That is not new, since he missed Wednesday’s practice last week before practicing fully on Friday and starting against the Tennessee Titans. If he cannot go, Luke Wypler would likely start at center, as he did against Pittsburgh in Week 4. There was encouraging news on the interior of the defensive line. Hall was limited with an ankle injury, a sign that he is getting closer after missing several weeks, and Graham was also limited with an ankle injury. Delpit was limited with a neck injury after clearing the concussion protocol last week. Schwesinger was limited with the same ankle injury he played through against Baltimore and Tennessee. Sampson, Harden and Thomas were also limited. Denzel Ward and Quincy Williams are not on the report after both were listed as questionable last week, which is good news for Cleveland’s defense. The Steelers have issues of their own. Cornerbacks Jalen Ramsey and Brandin Echols missed practice with wrist and hamstring injuries, and edge rusher Alex Highsmith was limited with a groin injury. Key contributors are back on the field, but they are still not out of the weeds yet, with one surprising player listed as questionable who can influence the outcome in Nashville. Denzel Ward was listed as questionable with a hand injury on Friday’s report. He was limited at practice on Friday, and the defense needs him to be healthy. Ward is having an incredible season locking down the offense’s top receiver. Another concerning, questionable designation is Quincy Williams with a neck injury. He has been flying around the field in recent weeks, making big hits and causing fumbles. Williams will be key to rushing Cameron Ward and forcing him to make bad decisions leading to errant throws and turnovers. However, Carson Schwesinger is in the lineup and he is so good that he can make up for Williams’ absence should he be out for the game. The defense continues to be hobbled as Grant Delpit is also listed as questionable with a concussion. He left last week’s game early with the injury, but has not been ruled for this week. The Browns’ stagnant rushing game will get a boost as Dylan Sampson has been upgraded to questionable. He suffered an injury in the first game of the season and has been out since. The defensive line gets a major boost with the return of Mason Graham. His injury in Week 4 looked bad, but he avoided the worst-case scenario and is back in the lineup after missing two games. picks.blurb: Early odds and bold Parker Washington prediction for Colts vs. Jaguars in Week 8 Skip to main content News FanSided NFL Sites Even though the Jacksonville Jaguars didn't play in Week 7, they managed to gain ground in the AFC South , as every other team in the division lost. The Jags are back from their break and will have a prime opportunity to keep building their lead when they play the hapless Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. The Colts are 2-5 and currently showing no signs of getting better this season. Heck, they let everyone know that they're punting on the season when they ousted general manager Chris Ballard, who failed to replenish the Indianapolis roster and left it devoid of talent. Following the dismissal of Ballard, Indy has gone on to hold a fire sale, sending All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks in return for a 2027 third-round pick and a fifth in 2028 days before the Jaguars game. While the Nelson trade could incentivize the Jags to make a push for defensive tackle DeForest Buckner , they cannot lose sight of the task at hand, which is beating the dreaded divisional foe. And with this in mind, here are the early odds for Week 8 and a bold Parker Washington prediction. The Colts vs. the Jaguars early odds for Week 8 The game will be held at EverBank Stadium, where the Colts have lost 11 consecutive games. Not surprisingly, the Jaguars are a 7.5-point favorite with a moneyline of -395 , via DraftKings. Bet $395 on them to win $100 if they beat Indianapolis for a total payout of $495. The Colts' moneyline sits at +310. Place a wager of $100 and win $310 if they beat Jacksonville for a total payout of $410. The over/under for the game is set at 49.5 points. ** Keep in mind that odds are refreshed periodically, so they can change at any moment. You may also like: 5 Jaguars who need to step up after the bye Bold Parker Washington prediction for the Jaguars vs. the Colts One of the biggest storylines surrounding the Jaguars in the offseason was that they opted not to make a big splash in free agency because they wanted to take care of their homegrown talent. Thus far, they locked up long snapper Ross Matiscik, defensive end Travon Walker, cornerback Montaric Brown, and tight end Brenton Strange, so you could make the case that general manager James Gladstone achieved the goal. That said, Parker Washington is still waiting on an extension. A sixth-round pick in 2023, Washington showed flashed his first two seasons but was stucked behind Christian Kirk. Jacksonville paved the way for him to start when Kirk was traded to the Houston Texans. Right off the bat, Washington became a key contributor on offense, registering 58 receptions for 807 yards with five touchdowns, all career bests, last year. Washington wasted no time picking up where he left off last year, racking up 26 receptions for 416 yards with four touchdowns. The former Penn State Nittany Lion is on pace to register the first 1,000-yard season of his career and should have no trouble getting the top-market contract he's been looking for . Although the Jags reportedly offered Washington $25 million per year before Week 1 , he rejected the offer. It's possible that he's aiming for an annual average of $30 million. Based on his production, he may be able to get it, and he'll have a prime opportunity when he plays the Colts. Already, Washington posted his first 100-yard game of the season against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 5. He'll get his second one in Week 8 when he registers seven receptions for a monster 140 yards with two touchdowns against Indy. away.headline: Quenton Nelson, Colts were close to a contract extension in the offseason, per report
away.blurb: In return for the All-Pro guard, the Colts received a 2027 third round pick and 2028 fifth round pick from Seattle. Nelson had reportedly wanted to sign a long-term contract extension to remain with the Colts. In exchange for Nelson, Indianapolis received a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. After the Indianapolis Colts fired general manger Chris Ballard 10 days ago, it sent a ripple effect down the organization. Coming off a second-half letdown and loss to the then 0-5 Tennessee Titans , it seemed clear that changes were imminent. Tuesday, the Colts traded Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks , a franchise cornerstone on the offensive line since Indianapolis drafted him with the No. 6 pick in the 2018 NFL Draft . With uncertainty surrounding the future of the organization, rumors began to swirl about trade requests regarding some of the Colts' most important players. ESPN NFL insider Ian Rapoport joined the Pat McAfee show Wednesday and shed some light on Nelson's situation in Indianapolis. "Is that accurate? He wanted to get a deal done with Indianapolis this off-season," McAfee asked Rapoport. "Yeah, that is true." Rapoport replied. "When Chris Ballard was there, I really thought it was going to get done." Nelson didn't sign an extension. He is currently on the final year of a four-year, $80 million contract, his first large-scale extension following his rookie contract. According to Rapoport, it was up to Nelson if he would be spending the next several years with the Colts' organization. "This is a huge bounty for someone in the middle of the season," Rapoport added. "A lot of people wanted this guy that the Seahawks think is like really, really going to help their run game." Since arriving in Indianapolis, Nelson was selected to the Pro Bowl each of his eight seasons and was named an All-Pro in six of those. Just a short time after Nelson's trade, the Colts moved another key piece of the roster in DeForest Buckner , who returns to the organization that drafted him, the San Francisco 49ers . Indianapolis received a 2027 fourth-round pick. With uncertainty surrounding the organization, there is reason to believe the roster moves won't stop here. Nonetheless, it was an offensive pillar that may have set off a revolving door of player personnel in Indianapolis. We may earn a commission when you buy through links on this page. away.headline: Jaguars-Colts Wednesday injury report: It is time to unleash Jalen Huskey
away.blurb: Johnson was the only Jaguar who did not practice Wednesday, which is not a great sign coming off a bye week. Johnson injured his ankle in the Week 6 loss to the Houston Texans in London, and the Jaguars very well may be without their best safety once they kick off against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. Limited in practice for the Jaguars were four players: linebacker Jalani Tavai (hamstring), wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring), long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder), and defensive tackle Ruke Orhorhoro. JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- There should be one clear reaction to the Jacksonville Jaguars' first injury report of Week 8: it is time for Jalen Huskey. Huskey, the No. 100 pick in April's NFL Draft, has yet to log a snap on defense and has only been active for one game. But the Jaguars should use this week to push Huskey toward some real playing time considering starting safety Antonio Johnson missed Wednesday's practice with an ankle injury. With second-year safety Caleb Ransaw on injured reserve and not looking close to returning anytime soon, the Jaguars' options at safety while Johnson recovers are starting safety Eric Murray, backup safety Kaevon Merriweather, second-year special teamer Rayuan Lane, or Huskey. The Jaguars leaned toward Merriweather getting playing time over Huskey at previous points, but it is time for the Jaguars to unleash their rookie. Merriweather has played 45 NFL games and has been in the NFL since 2023, so naturally he has more experience than Huskey does just a few months into his NFL career. But the Jaguars need to see what they have in their young safety, especially as injuries continue to hit the safety room. Even if the Jaguars start Merriweather over Huskey, they should deploy their third-round defensive back as their No. 3 safety. Simply put, Jacksonville has a young, athletic and talented safety who has been waiting in the wings, and it is time to see what he has. That is not to say Huskey would be the solution to the Jaguars' issues with explosive passes allowed, but he would give the Jaguars a dynamic at the safety position that Lane and Merriweather likely would not. Johnson not playing on Sunday would be a significant blow for the Jaguars' defense considering the impact he has made this season, both in coverage and as a blitzer against the run and rushing the passer. But the Jaguars drafted Huskey for situations like this, and it is time to let him play. With that said, there was some good news for the Jaguars on the injury front. Cornerback Montaric Brown was a full participant after missing time with a hamstring injury that has sidelined him for all but six snaps in the Jaguars' last three games. Brown was struggling at times before his injury, but a healthy Brown would help change the math in the cornerback room and potentially allow the Jaguars to play Jarrian Jones in the slot more than he has played since Brown started missing practice and game reps due to injury. home.headline: Jaguars-Colts Wednesday injury report: It is time to unleash Jalen Huskey
home.blurb: Johnson was the only Jaguar who did not practice Wednesday, which is not a great sign coming off a bye week. Johnson injured his ankle in the Week 6 loss to the Houston Texans in London, and the Jaguars very well may be without their best safety once they kick off against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. Limited in practice for the Jaguars were four players: linebacker Jalani Tavai (hamstring), wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring), long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder), and defensive tackle Ruke Orhorhoro. JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- There should be one clear reaction to the Jacksonville Jaguars' first injury report of Week 8: it is time for Jalen Huskey. Huskey, the No. 100 pick in April's NFL Draft, has yet to log a snap on defense and has only been active for one game. But the Jaguars should use this week to push Huskey toward some real playing time considering starting safety Antonio Johnson missed Wednesday's practice with an ankle injury. With second-year safety Caleb Ransaw on injured reserve and not looking close to returning anytime soon, the Jaguars' options at safety while Johnson recovers are starting safety Eric Murray, backup safety Kaevon Merriweather, second-year special teamer Rayuan Lane, or Huskey. The Jaguars leaned toward Merriweather getting playing time over Huskey at previous points, but it is time for the Jaguars to unleash their rookie. Merriweather has played 45 NFL games and has been in the NFL since 2023, so naturally he has more experience than Huskey does just a few months into his NFL career. But the Jaguars need to see what they have in their young safety, especially as injuries continue to hit the safety room. Even if the Jaguars start Merriweather over Huskey, they should deploy their third-round defensive back as their No. 3 safety. Simply put, Jacksonville has a young, athletic and talented safety who has been waiting in the wings, and it is time to see what he has. That is not to say Huskey would be the solution to the Jaguars' issues with explosive passes allowed, but he would give the Jaguars a dynamic at the safety position that Lane and Merriweather likely would not. Johnson not playing on Sunday would be a significant blow for the Jaguars' defense considering the impact he has made this season, both in coverage and as a blitzer against the run and rushing the passer. But the Jaguars drafted Huskey for situations like this, and it is time to let him play. With that said, there was some good news for the Jaguars on the injury front. Cornerback Montaric Brown was a full participant after missing time with a hamstring injury that has sidelined him for all but six snaps in the Jaguars' last three games. Brown was struggling at times before his injury, but a healthy Brown would help change the math in the cornerback room and potentially allow the Jaguars to play Jarrian Jones in the slot more than he has played since Brown started missing practice and game reps due to injury. home.headline: Vega Ioane's injury could give Jaguars' D-line a sudden edge against Ravens
home.blurb: Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Ioane suffered an MCL sprain, adding that he'll miss time even though it's a short-term injury. The rookie hog molly left the loss to the Cincinnati Bengals and didn't return. It's hard to tell just how much time is a little time, but if it wasn't serious, Ioane would be week-to-week or questionable for Week 8. He's not, meaning that there's a strong chance he won't suit up against Jacksonville. Following their BYE, the Jacksonville Jaguars will face the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8 . And after their AFC showdown, they'll face off against the Baltimore Ravens. While it's hard to tell if Lamar Jackson will suit up for the game — he's seemingly dealing with a high-ankle sprain — the Jags now know that they probably won't have to face rookie offensive guard Vega Ioane. The Jaguars may not have to worry about Vega Ioane when they play the Ravens The Jaguars will face Baltimore in Week 9. It will be a Thursday Night game. Given that there's a three-day gap between Sunday games and Thursday, players who don't suit up Sunday often miss the Thursday bout. That doesn't bode well for Vega Ioane's availability. A first-round pick of the Ravens in 2026, Ioane got off to a strong start to his rookie season, giving up just one sack and eight total pressures in six games. Ioane began the season at right guard but eventually moved to center. He returned to right guard when Baltimore traded for Cam Jurgens from the Philadelphia Eagles. Emery Jones Jr. may be the next man up. You may also like: AFC South Week 8 power ranking: The Jags win big without playing The Jaguars' D-Line must take advantage of Vega Ioane's absence Lamar Jackson has missed three games with injuries . Tyler Huntley has filled in for him, throwing for 664 yards with four touchdowns and one interception during his absence. There hasn't been that steep a drop-off at quarterback, but without Vega Ioane, the Baltimore offensive line could have trouble protecting whoever lines up behind center. This is encouraging news for a Jacksonville defensive line that has struggled to create pressure from the interior. While the Jaguars excel at stuffing the run, they have had trouble getting after the quarterback this season, registering just 11 sacks. Sure, they've racked up pressures, but those haven't always translated into big plays, takeaways, and such. Maybe the Jags can get better production from their interior defensive line after their break. Arik Armstead has played at a high level at times but has been inconsistent. On the other hand, DaVon Hamilton won't offer much in the pass-rush department, while Ruke Orhorhoro hasn't made the leap he was expected to make when he was traded to Jacksonville. Rookie Albert Regis is also in the mix but has barely played. When you add it all up, it's easy to see why the Jaguars are being urged to trade for a defensive tackle . Maybe they will, maybe they won't, but they'll at least get a bit of a break when they play the Rave

picks.headline: Week 8 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Chiefs look to bounce back vs. Broncos
picks.blurb: Week 8 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Chiefs look to bounce back vs. Broncos - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football TNF preview: Panthers vs. Packers WNBA Finals: Dream force Game 7 Brewers win World Series Celebrate, Milwaukee! Dybantsa delivers in debut Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, October 29, 2026 at 3:49 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the Denver Broncos, Week 1 had to feel like a bad flashback. The first 12 times that Patrick Mahomes started against the Broncos, the Kansas City Chiefs won every time. Then there was a shift with Sean Payton in charge, and the Broncos won two of three against Mahomes and the Chiefs. The 2026 season opener, though, was like old times. It wasn't Mahomes that ruined the Broncos in the opener, though he played pretty well. It was Kenneth Walker III doing most of the damage, as he ran through many Denver missed tackles for 173 rushing yards. Also, the Chiefs' defense shut down Denver in a 31-10 win. It was a complete, impressive performance. It doesn't seem like much has changed since then. The Chiefs started 5-0 before losing last week at Seattle, a very tough opponent. The Broncos are 5-2 but questions persist about their offense. While the defense on the whole has been better for the Broncos, the run defense isn't great. Denver is 26th in EPA ( expected points added ) per rush allowed. It's easy to say that the Seahawks showed everyone how to beat the Chiefs — take Walker out of the game — but not everyone has Seattle's defense to pull that off. The Broncos showed once they aren't a great matchup against Walker. That's a big reason Kansas City -1.5 is the pick. We saw in the season opener that the Chiefs' dominance over the Broncos might not be over. Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III had 173 rushing yards in Week 1 against the Broncos. (AP Photo/Colin E. Braley) Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 8 of the NFL season: Panthers (+3.5) over Packers There's no way the Panthers are as bad as they played last week, when they were down 33-6 to the Buccaneers by halftime. Competent teams that get embarrassed usually bounce back well. The Packers are still a tough team to predict. Raiders (+1.5) over Jets The early East Coast start has been death for the Raiders for a long time, but they are probably the better team. They are certainly the better coached team. The Raiders are on a four-game losing streak but look at the opponents: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills, Rams. Those are four of the strongest teams in the NFL. If Las Vegas can't win here, it might be Fernando Mendoza time. Cowboys (-6.5) over Cardinals The Cowboys are going to score. The Cardinals have given up at least 30 points in six of their eight games. Dallas showed on Monday night that its offense is back, but what about the defense? Maybe a strong fourth quarter against the Eagles is a sign that the Cowboys' defense can be somewhat competent. It's scary to pick the Dallas laying points to anyone because they'll need to get stops, but it would be a surprise if they don't score 30. Buccaneers (-2.5) over Falcons Good luck figuring out either of these teams. The Buccaneers could be better than we think. Their only significant weakness has been pass offense, and that is explained by having an undrafted rookie starting three of their seven games. We don't know if Baker Mayfield is fully healthy, considering he had just 11 pass attempts in his return from a dislocated right thumb last week, but if he is maybe the Bucs can get on a roll. Browns (+3.5) over Steelers Teams coming back from an international game and playing right away without a bye are 0-3-1 this season. The losses were by 12, 11, and 6 points, and the close loss was by the Texans as a 10-point favorite last week. The tie was the Commanders when they were favored at home against the Giants. It's a hard turnaround, and it's what the Steelers face coming back from Paris last Sunday. Both of these teams are 5-2 but flawed, and I'll ride with the angle of the Browns not being the team that played in France last week. Jaguars (-9.5) over Colts It's hard to imagine being a Colts player this week. Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were traded and everyone else with any value has to wonder if they're next. It's actually surprising the line is less than 10 points against a Jaguars team coming off a bye and a loss. This one could get really ugly. The remainder of the Colts' season could get really ugly. Ravens (+3.5) over Bills You've seen this here before: This all depends on if Lamar Jackson plays. This week, I assume he will. It seemed like he was close last week and he practiced in full on Wednesday. There would be some real frustration if he's not back for this game, which Baltimore might need to win to start to save its season. The Ravens' remaining schedule is the toughest in the NFL, according to DVOA . If he does play, we know the Bills defense is not very good. Getting more than a field goal seems good. Vikings (+3.5) over Lions If the Vikings' build was reversed, and they had a fun offense that was clearly one of the two best in the sport but a defense that was unreliable and among the 10 worst in the NFL, we'd respect them more. How do we know that? The 2026 Buffalo Bills, that's how. Minnesota's defense has been remarkable. Look at the Chicago Bears this season. In three of Caleb Williams' four starts, Chicago is averaging 39 points. In the other start, against the Vikings, the Bears scored three points at home (Williams got injured in that game but not until the middle of the fourth quarter). Maybe Detroit will figure out Brian Flores' defense, but nobody else has and I'm willing to take more than a field goal with the Vikings. Titans (+10.5) over Bengals The Titans have been blown out only twice. They lost by 13 to the Jets in Week 1 and 23 to the Texans in Week 5. Every other game has been decided by six or fewer points. The Titans have won only one of those games, but they're keeping it close. It's possible Joe Burrow will add to his growing MVP argument and torch Tennessee in a blowout, but this seems like a good spot for an ugly underdog. Rams (-6.5) over Chargers Typically, an 0-6 team coming off a bye would be a fine choice. The Chargers don't want to get embarrassed all season, but they're simply not a good team in any phase. That is shocking but also irrefutable. This is the exact type of contrarian pick I'd like to make but I just can't get there with the Chargers. Patriots (-7) over Dolphins It's possible the Dolphins get some confidence from their first win. It's also possible they let down a bit: It's still a 1-5 team whose goal was to get that first win out of the way. On the other side, there's a Patriots team coming off a loss with three extra days of rest. Commanders (-5.5) over Eagles A low point of this week was looking at the schedule and realizing this was the Sunday night game. Not fun. Not sure what's more surprising: That a 1-4-1 Commanders team is a 5.5-point favorite over the Eagles, or that the Commanders are the pick. The Eagles' best remaining effort was going to come on a Monday night against the rival Cowboys, and that effort was pretty meager. It won't get better. Bears (+3) over Seahawks The Sunday night game might not be good, but Monday night makes up for it. This one is fun (and should have been the Week 1 opener, but that's an old gripe). If there's an offensive coach that can figure out the Seahawks' defense, it's Ben Johnson. Caleb Williams has been on a heater since returning from a hamstring injury. Win the turnover battle As we saw in the Thursday night win over the Seattle Seahawks, when the Broncos defense creates turnovers and the offense protects the ball, Denver wins. The Broncos have been better at creating takeaways this season, and they need to carry that over on Sunday. Force Mahomes into some rushed throws and/or punch the ball out to give Bo Nix and the offense some added possessions. On top of that, Nix and the offense need to continue to protect the ball. picks.blurb: 1. With Kenneth Walker III coming to town, the Broncos will be called on to clean up an operation that missed 28 tackles in the Chiefs' season-opening romp. Kansas City surely wants to get the Super Bowl 60 MVP back to his early-season form after the Seahawks kept him in check. Denver has shown signs in recent weeks of its run defense coalescing, but Sunday will mark a stiff test after the group overwhelmed shorthanded backfields in the last two weeks. 2. Injuries loom large in the matchup between the Chiefs' aerial attack and the Broncos' vaunted pass defense. Getting receiver Rashee Rice and right tackle Jaylon Moore back could provide a significant boost to a Kansas City attack coming off arguably the worst offensive outing of Patrick Mahomes' tenure. But Denver could also get significant reinforcements with cornerback Patrick Surtain II trying to play after sitting out three weeks with an ankle injury. 3. A methodical Denver offense finally found its explosive streak last week against Arizona, with Bo Nix and RJ Harvey both reeling off long touchdowns. Repeating that effort against the Chiefs could be difficult, especially with Jaylen Waddle's status in question after he suffered a chest injury late against Arizona. But the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman, who had 93 rushing yards in his first game back from injured reserve, could help the Broncos avoid the obvious passing situations that plagued the team early in the season. The Chiefs have their own issues to sort through, and the Week 1 blowout doesn't tell us how this rematch will unfold. We should get a considerably tighter game, with both defenses making the offenses work. I'm not sure I trust Patrick Mahomes, given the lack of quality pass-catchers around him, but I do trust Kenneth Walker III against one of the NFL's worst run defenses on the heels of a homecoming dud. A rout similar to Week 1 might not be in the cards, but Kansas City should be able to escape with the sweep. Kansas City is coming off its first loss of the season, while Denver has won three straight and can move ahead of the Chiefs in the division with a victory. The teams met in the season opener on September 14 at Arrowhead Stadium. The Chiefs rolled to a 31-10 win, outgaining Denver 392 yards – 176 yards. Patrick Mahomes threw two touchdown passes and ran for another score, but the star of the night was offseason addition Kenneth Walker III who gashed Denver for 173 rushing yards and a touchdown on 23 carries. The Chiefs arrive in Denver looking to rebound from their 20-3 loss at Seattle last weekend, a game in which they were simply outclassed as Mahomes and co. never found a rhythm. Kansas City managed only 213 total yards and 11 first downs and failed to reach the red zone, while Mahomes completed 19 of 33 passes for 165 yards with no touchdowns and an interception. Walker, facing his former team, was held to just 36 yards on 14 carries after entering the night averaging a league-leading 133 rushing yards per game. Seattle controlled the ball for nearly 36 minutes, converted 11 of 16 third downs and got 150 receiving yards and a touchdown from Jaxon Smith-Njigba . Even when Kansas City had chances to get back into the game, Harrison Butker missed field goals from 58 and 45 yards, leaving the Chiefs with only a third-quarter field goal. Denver, meanwhile, enters with momentum after a 30-16 road win over Arizona. Bo Nix supplied the game’s biggest play with a career-long 62-yard touchdown run late in the second quarter and finished with 222 passing yards and 73 rushing yards, while RJ Harvey turned a screen pass into a 52-yard touchdown and J.K. Dobbins added a one-yard score. The Broncos’ defense repeatedly disrupted Jacoby Brissette and the Cardinals’ offense, producing 12 quarterback hits, six tackles for loss and three sacks. Kansas City owns a 74-59 all-time advantage and dominated Denver with a 16-game winning streak from 2015 through 2023, including Mahomes winning his first 12 starts against the Broncos. Denver finally broke that run in 2023 and has since shown it can compete with KC, but the Chiefs reasserted themselves emphatically with September’s 31-10 victory. away.headline: Chiefs Dealt Costly Injury Blow That Could Test Patrick Mahomes Against Seahawks
away.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs have listed five players on their injury report ahead of Sunday Night Football against the Seattle Seahawks . Three players have been ruled out, while two remain questionable for the matchup. Chiefs rule out players as others remain questionable According to the Kansas City Chiefs , five players are listed on the injury report ahead of Sunday Night Football against the Seattle Seahawks. L'Jarius Sneed and Cooper McDonald are questionable, while Rashee Rice, Jaylon Moore and Brashard Smith are out. Left tackle Josh Simmons was previously placed on injured reserve with a back injury . Sneed and McDonald are both dealing with knee injuries. Sneed was limited in practice throughout the week, leaving his availability for the game against Seattle uncertain. McDonald is also listed as questionable because of his knee injury. He was designated to return from injured reserve on October 20 and has participated in limited practices since then. Moore has been ruled out because of a concussion. The offensive tackle missed practice while dealing with the injury, creating an opening along the offensive line. Joshua Ezeudu is a possible replacement at right tackle. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes has practiced fully and does not carry an injury designation for the game. Tight end Travis Kelce was limited in practice because of an ankle issue, but he also has no game designation. Both players are available for Sunday night's matchup. Rice, Moore and Smith have been ruled out, while Sneed and McDonald are listed as questionable. Kansas City will face Seattle at Lumen Field on Sunday night, with Kelce available despite limited participation in practice. away.headline: Week 7 Injury Report: Chiefs at Seahawks
away.blurb: The Seahawks will be without running back Zach Charbonnet for another game. Charbonnet, who is working his way back from the torn ACL he suffered in the Divisional Round of the playoffs, practiced fully this week, but has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs. Also ruled out for the Seahawks are linebacker Drake Thomas , who will be out for the second week in a row due to an ankle injury, and linebacker Chazz Surratt , who will be missing a fourth straight game with a calf injury. Among those listed as questionable for the Seahawks is safety Nick Emmanwori , who was a new addition to the injury report on Friday, listed as limited due to a hip. Also questionable are outside linebackers DeMarcus Lawrence (knee) and Uchenna Nwosu (hip), both of whom were limited for the second straight day, backup quarterback Drew Lock , who has been limited all week with a right elbow injury, and outside linebacker Connor O'Toole (hamstring), who was limited Friday after not practicing the previous two days. For the Chiefs, starting right tackle Jaylon Moore is out due to a concussion. Left tackle Josh Simmons, who already missed the first five games of the season with a back injury, was placed on injured reserve earlier this week. Also out for Kansas City are receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) and running back Brashard Smith (hamstring). For the Chiefs, cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (knee) and linebacker Cooper Macdonald (knee) are both listed as questionable after being limited in Friday's practice. home.headline: Broncos' first injury report for Week 8 paints an early bleak picture
home.blurb: Of note, Patrick Surtain II pracitced in full, so the Broncos should get him back, but all of Allen, Waddle, and Talanoa Hufanga did not practice: The initial report with Waddle was that he aggravated his chest injury, but that there is 'hope' he can play on Sunday. Hufanga has already missed a couple of games due to his ankle injury, and if he does not practice in some capacity on Thursday, his status for Week 8 is in doubt. Allen has a hamstring injury and did not practice, either. The weird thing is that there was not any sort of report that came out with Allen's injury like we saw with Waddle, so that could end up being good news that it's pretty minor. We're definitely not going to make any declarations here since it's early in the week, but the Thursday statuses are going to be huge, as if any of the three "DNP" players from Wednesday are limited or full on Thursday, their chances of playing go way up. Sean Payton hilariously called himself out for awful Jaylen Waddle play call The Denver Broncos have consistently been among the healthiest teams in the NFL since Sean Payton took over back in 2023. That doesn't mean, though, the team has not dealt with injuries. Every NFL team has to deal with injuries in some capacity, and the teams that are usually standing in the end have better depth or better roster health overall. In Week 7, a win over the Arizona Cardinals, the Broncos saw two key players leave the game in wide receiver Jaylen Waddle, and defensive end Zach Allen. And in the team's first injury report of Week 8, we see some key players on the report, and while it is early, their statuses for Week 8 could already be in doubt. Denver Broncos injury report is getting longer as Week 8 approaches However, if any of them again do not practice on Thursday, it would logically be unlikely that they play on Sunday. While the Broncos are more talented than Kansas City and get this game at home, not having even one of these players is going to be brutal. In the same way that 2025's home game against the Chiefs was important, this one is as well. The Broncos would be in first place in the AFC West with a win, but if they lose, the Chiefs would improve to 6-1, and Denver would drop to 5-3 with two losses to the Chiefs already etched into their record. It would severely hurt their chances at repeating as division champions. And as it concerns the pasing game, if the Broncos hope to build on their breakout from Week 7, having Waddle in the lineup would allow that to continue to happen. home.blurb: Denver listed wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest), safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), and defensive end Zach Allen (hip) — all starters — as "DNP" (Did Not Practice) following Wednesday's session. Hufanga remains on the wrong side of questionable after missing the last two games due to an ankle injury. The former AFC Defensive Player of the Week will need to get in at least limited practices on Thursday and Friday to have a shot at suiting up versus Kansas City. Allen's apparently hamstring ailment is a new development, though one that, as of this writing, seems unlikely to hold him out of Week 8 action. Elsewhere on the injury report, left tackle Garett Bolles (hip) and wide receiver Marvin Mims (ankle) were considered limited, while cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle), defensive tackle Malcolm Roach (neck), and inside linebacker Karene Reid (elbow) were full participants. Surtain appears poised to return from a three-game absence as his ankle presumably is at or near full health. "Obviously as a returner, that first return with the ball midfield, those are... I’ve said this before, the receiving now to start the game. [At] minimum there’s a threshold, but to start where we started, those are things that he’s shown us consistently. He continues to have those touches and then where you want to even get him more touches. It’s sometimes a challenge, but certainly he’s deserving.” The Denver Broncos released their initial Week 8 injury report ahead of Sunday's pivotal home showdown against the Kansas City Chiefs. An earlier report indicated that Waddle suffered a re-aggravation of a prior chest issue toward the end of last week's victory over the Arizona Cardinals, and his status for Sunday's game is to be determined. The injury occurred on a trick play that head coach and offensive playcaller Sean Payton consequently apologized for. "Why didn't anybody ask me about the dumb reverse call? ... It was awful. I'm sorry," Payton said in his postgame press conference on Sunday. "If you look it up, in 2008, in a similar situation — even a more radical reverse — fumbled, Tampa Bay beat us. I know better. New England’s three-game winning streak ended in a 30-24 loss at Chicago last Thursday, despite Drake Maye completing 24 of 31 passes for 321 yards and two touchdowns while also rushing for a score. The loss can be attributed to a costly interception from Maye in the red zone in the second quarter and New England compounded it with 10 penalties and a defense that missed 16 tackles. Miami, meanwhile, is coming off its best afternoon of the season, a 28-25 road victory over the Jets on October 25 that gave coach Jeff Hafley his first win and kept the Dolphins from starting 0-6. Malik Willis was the catalyst, completing 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns to rookie Caleb Douglas , adding 37 rushing yards and another score, and converting a game-clinching fourth-and-1 in the final two minutes. Miami scored touchdowns on three of its first four possessions and led 21-7 at halftime before a late Jets comeback made things interesting. Ollie Gordon II rushed for 103 yards and a touchdown, while Douglas’ 63-yard fourth-quarter catch-and-run provided the winning points. This rivalry has swung toward New England recently after several seasons in which Miami consistently gave the Patriots problems. The teams’ most recent meeting came January 4, 2026, when New England completed a season sweep with a dominant 38-10 victory at Gillette Stadium to finish the 2025 regular season 14-3. Rhamondre Stevenson was the centerpiece, rushing seven times for 131 yards and two touchdowns and catching another touchdown from Maye, while TreVeyon Henderson added two rushing scores; Maye finished 14 of 18 for 191 yards and a touchdown before exiting early in the fourth quarter. Keep an eye on Saquon: Speaking of injuries, Saquon Barkley played only nine snaps Monday while dealing with hamstring and back issues. He offered an encouraging assessment of his hamstring and said he doesn't expect the back problem to keep him out. His practice workload still warrants watching. 3. The preparation advantage favors Washington: The Commanders come off their bye, while the Eagles turn around from Monday night for a Sunday road game. That's valuable extra time to prepare for Tanner McKee and the Eagles' reshuffled offense. 4. McKee needs help from his defense: Philadelphia's quarterback threw for 211 yards, one touchdown and one interception against Dallas. The Eagles produced three touchdown drives, but their defense couldn't slow the Cowboys. Sustaining drives only helps so much if the other team keeps answering. 5. away.blurb: Dallas Goedert is good to go for Monday, while Saquon Barkley and Jalyx Hunt inch closer to a potential return. "It's just kind of the same injury that I sustained earlier. I just had a little bit of inflammation in there, had to let that settle down, but felt really good running out there today," Goedert said after Saturday's practice. "I want to be out there anytime I can. We only get 17 games. To miss a game, to miss two games, it always stinks. So if I can be available, I'm going to do everything I can to play. "I'm going to go out there and do whatever I can to help the team win, whether it's run blocking, pass blocking, or hopefully get a couple catches. We're looking forward to this game playing on Monday night against the division rival. It's going to be a lot of fun. The atmosphere's going to be great and it's a game I wouldn't want to miss." Two of the Eagles' top receivers, DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), have been ruled out, leaving rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon as the primary wide receiver option. "It's definitely a big opportunity with the team," Lemon said. "I'm just super excited to go out there with the guys, put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys. So, just trying to go out there and execute. A couple guys are out. So really just, next man up. I got a bunch of trust in the guys next to me, trust in the coaches and the game plan." Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) took a step forward and was a full participant at practice on Saturday after being limited previously in the week. The running back is listed as questionable for Monday night. Meanwhile, Jonathan Greenard (ankle), who did not practice again on Saturday, is listed as questionable. The edge rusher said it will be a game-time decision as he will need to see how his ankle feels. Alongside Greenard, the outside linebacker room is banged up. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) could return on Monday as he is listed as questionable after practicing in a limited capacity all week. Nolan Smith (concussion) has been officially ruled out. Smith is joined by defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett, tight end Grant Calcaterra, guard Landon Dickerson, and tight end Eli Stowers all participated fully in practice on Saturday. They are all listed as questionable since they are on Injured Reserve and would need to be activated by Monday afternoon in order to play against the Cowboys. home.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles opened their Week 8 preparations Wednesday with an extensive injury report, listing six players as nonparticipants and another six as limited participants ahead of Sunday's NFC East matchup against the Washington Commanders . Barkley's status remains one of the biggest concerns after the veteran suffered a back injury during Monday night's 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. The Eagles listed him with hamstring and back injuries Wednesday, adding another concern for a player who recently returned from a hamstring issue that kept him out of consecutive games. Barkley opened the Dallas matchup with a 29-yard run and scored a touchdown on Philadelphia's first possession, but his workload was limited after his back tightened. He eventually left the game, forcing the Eagles to rely on their remaining running backs. Lemon responded with his first career touchdown reception against the Cowboys, but the Eagles would benefit from having additional receiving options available against Washington. Campbell was listed as a nonparticipant with hamstring and quadriceps injuries, adding to concerns for a defense that struggled against Dallas. Jones was sidelined by a hamstring injury, while Covey was listed with a knee injury after leaving Monday night's game. The defensive injury situation extends beyond those six players. Outside linebackers Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt and Nolan Smith were all listed as limited participants, along with defensive backs Michael Carter II, linebacker Smael Mondon Jr. and defensive tackle Moro Ojomo. The Eagles return to practice Thursday, and actual participation should better indicate which players are progressing toward Sunday's game. They hit road to play the Super Bowl-champion Seattle Seahawks. And they'll do it with a brand new All-Pro defensive tackle! Jeffery Simmons is a Bear! The Bears are proving themselves to be one of the best offenses in the league with one of the best rising-star quarterbacks. And their head coach and quarterback face a huge test against one of the league's best defenses. Chicago didn't fare so well in their first defensive test of the year, against the Minnesota Vikings. However, the weather was a factor in that game, like it or not. Plus, Caleb Williams didn't finish the game. Excuses, maybe, but also realities. This matchup has a lot of great storylines and will be a measuring stick for the Bears to see how they compete against the league's best. It feels like a game with playoff implications. It feels like a game worthy of the Monday Night Football spotlight. It will be the first game in November for the Bears, too. When teams really start to separate themselves. Let's meet the Seahawks. Seattle Seahawks SB Nation site : Field Gulls Record: 4-3, second in the NFC West Last week: 20-3 win over the Kansas City Chiefs Game day, time, TV: Monday, 7:15 p.m. CT, ESPN Spread: Seattle -3.5 Bears all-time record against: 8-12, including 2-0 postseason Historical meeting: The Bears have never beaten the Seahawks in the month of November. In the second-ever meeting between the teams, the Seahawks beat the Bears 31-29 in week 10 of 1978. The Bears fell behind 21-9 with Jim Zorn hitting Steve Largent twice for touchdowns and Sherman Smith rushing for another. But Chicago made a strong comeback. Roland Harper scored on a 20-yard pass from Mike Phipps. After another Smith touchdown, Walter Payton scored from 7 yards out, drawing the Bears within six. The Seahawks drove down the field and tacked on another field goal to go up 31-22. Phipps threw a pick but Sam McCullum intercepted Zorn right back. Phipps put together a good drive and Harper scored a 2-yard TD with 40 seconds left. The Bears managed to recover the onside kick but with 12 seconds left, from Seattle's 46-yard line, Phipps' pass was intercepted to end the game. Last meeting: Who could forget the awful, terrible 6-3 Thursday Night Football game? Thomas Brown was coaching the Bears. It was a defensive slugfest. Or a total offensive mess. Depends on how you remember it. The most memorable play didn't count, as Caleb Williams rolled out and threw an off-platform pass to Rome Odunze four a touchdown. It was called back for offensive holding. (I cannot find a clip online, but I remember it was awesome). Offense: The Seahawks offense ranks 13th in points and 15th in yards. Their passing offense is 16th and their rushing offense ranks 17th. Sam Darnold (62.1 pct. cmp./1,290 yds./8 TD/8 INT) currently leads the league in interceptions, but played a lot better last week. Unless you've been living under a rock, you likely know about Jaxon Smith-Njigba (58 rec./867 yds./8 TD). Beyond him are AJ Barner (19/180/0), Cooper Kupp (18/199/1), deep threat Rashid Shaheed (16/163/0) and George Holani (12/88/0). Jadarian Price (28 att./119 yds./0 TD) is injured, but expected to return to practice this week along with Zach Charbonnett (no stats in 2026 yet). In their absence, it's been Emanuel Wilson (111 att./403 yds./3 TD) and Holani (26/108/1). Defense: Seattle's defense comes into Monday night as one the league's best. They rank fourth in points allowed and first in yards allowed. Their passing defense ranks first in passing yards and sixth in rushing. The loaded unit stars Nick Emmanwori (27 tkls/3 TFL/2 sk/1 PD/7 QB hits), DTs Leonard Williams (3 sk/7 TFL/9 QB hits/1 PD), Byron Murphy (3 sk/ 24 tkls/5 TFL/6 QB hits) Derick Hall (3 sk/19 QB hits/3 TFL/1 FF/1 FR) and Ernest Jones (3 sk/68 tkls/3 TFL/2 QB hits/1 INT/3 PD) and Devon Witherspoon (41 tkls/3 PD/3 TFL/1 QB hits) Other playmakers are Julian Love (2 INT/6 PD/24 tkls/2 TFL), Nehemiah Pritchett (13 tkls/4 PD/2 INT) and Josh Jobe (27 tkls/1 PD/1 INT/1 TFL). Key matchups: This is a top offense against a top defense. The Bears are going to have to play disciplined football. Take what their given, take shots when they can, use play-action to suck in the LBs. On defense, stop JSN. That's no easy task. The Seahawks can find a running game if Price and/or Charbonnett are back. Anyway to get pressure on Sam Darnold is good though; we know what happens when he is pressured. The Seahawks haven't allowed a 300-yard passer this season. The Rams are the only team with more than 300 passing yards against Seattle since week 2 of last season. Seattle has lost only three times at home going back to the beginning of last season. The 49ers are the only team to beat Seattle at home during this span Despite their strong numbers, the Seahawks have allowed opponents to score on 78.6 percent of their trips inside of the red zone. The Seahawks' 13 offensive turnovers on the season rank fourth-most in the league. Their 12 defensive turnovers rank third-most. Seattle is allowing a league-low 144.4 passing yards per game and the second-worst passer rating of 72.6. Only the Vikings allow a worse QB rating Can the Bears hang with a team as good as the Seahawks? How will their offense and QB measure up against Seattle's defense?

Dybantsa delivers in debut Bears vs. Seahawks bold predictions for Week 8 Monday Night Football Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints Wed, October 28, 2026 at 11:24 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chicago Bears have demonstrated quite a bit of explosiveness this season, especially when Caleb Williams is under center and running back Kyle Monangai is healthy and in the lineup. Williams has been in the lineup for the past two games and has demonstrated no ill effects from the hamstring injury that sidelined him earlier in the year. Monangai has missed the last three games and while he is improving, there are no guarantees that he will be back in the lineup for this game. The Seahawks have not been at their best in the first half of the season and they take a 4-3 record into this home game. They are coming off a key Sunday night victory over the Kansas City Chiefs in which their defense performed at a peak level. They will need that kind of effort against the Bears. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Sam Darnold was one of the keys to Seattle's surge to last year's Super Bowl title. He has not been as efficient this season, as interceptions have been an issue. The Bears defense got a huge lift from their ability to create takeaways last year. They have not been as proficient in that area this season — minus-1 on the takeaway/turnover table — but they have been a middle-of-the-pack defense that has been moderately capable this season. This game could come down to turnover differential, and if the Bears are going to win on the road, they have to gain an advantage in this area. Williams will throw for 250 yards and 2 TDs Williams has demonstrated that he can rise to the occasion and handle pressure. He has an excellent partnership with head coach Ben Johnson, and it appears that those two will allow the Bears to remain contenders in the division and the NFC for several years. Williams has all the tools that an outstanding quarterback needs, and as the No. 1 selection in the 2024 NFL Draft, nearly all scouts and personnel specialists were predicting great things for him. However, Williams struggled in his rookie season under former head coach Matt Eberflus. That coach did not have the wherewithal to teach and demand outstanding play from Williams. However that changed under Johnson, and the quarterback reads and understands defenses, and he knows how to pick apart good defenses and make key plays. The one area that scouts did not get right about Williams was his speed and escapability from the pocket. He was thought to be above average or good in that area, and that assessment did not give him enough credit. He is sensational in that area. He has a strong partnership with wide receivers Rome Odunze and Luther Burden, as well as big-play tight end Colston Loveland. This trio should be able to cause problems for the Seattle defense, which is one of the strongest units in the league. Williams and the receivers will not overpower the Seahawks defense, but the quarterback will throw 2 TD passes and approach the 275-yard mark. Smith-Njigba is unstoppable, will exceed 125 yards and score a TD Mandatory Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images The Bears regularly have to contend with outstanding receivers like Justin Jefferson, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Christian Watson in the NFC North. However, Seattle wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is at another level. He is coming off a sensational game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Smith-Njigba was targeted 12 times by Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold and he caught 9 passes for 150 yards and 1 touchdown. The Chiefs knew he was the central point of the Seattle offensive game plan, yet defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo could not do anything to slow him down. Stopping him was out of the question. Chicago defensive coordinator Dennis Allen will face the same issue. Allen certainly knows what it is like to face outstanding wideouts in the NFC North, but Smith-Njigba may be too strong for the Bears defense. He has caught 58 passes for 867 yards and 8 TDs, and asking CBs Jaylon Johnson, Malik Muhammad and Kyler Gordon to prevent him from making big plays will be folly. The best way for the Bears to go about it would be pressuring Darnold and keep him from delivering accurate passes. The Bears have registered 19 sacks and Darnold has been trapped 14 times thus far. Allen's top priority will be to make sure his personnel gets in Darnold's face and prevents him from getting the ball to Smith-Njigba. That scenario is unlikely, but it is Chicago's best defensive hope. Bold game prediction: Seahawks 27, Bears 24 The Bears have the weapons to go into Seattle and give the defending champions a battle for 60 minutes. This is the kind of game that Johnson and Williams would like to use as a measuring stick. However, the Seahawks have already lost 3 games and they can't afford to lose any more. They will have a major challenge chasing down the 49ers in the NFC West, and dropping a home game to a solid team is not in their plans. The Seahawks played their best all-around game against the Chiefs in Week 7, and they will stay on track against the Bears. Seattle wins a close, well-played game against Williams and the Bears. away.blurb: Kyle Monangai inching closer to Bears return The Chicago Bears have been without Kyle Monangai for their last three games due to a turf toe injury. While the franchise has gone 2-1 in that span, the running back’s absence has been made painfully clear. In the four games he appeared in prior to his injury, Monangai turned 60 carries into 324 yards and three touchdowns. He picked up his injury after rushing 30 times for 146 yards and two touchdowns against the New York Jets. While his total rushing attempts skews the metric a tad, Monangai’s 5.4 yards per carry ranks third-best in the NFL. Head coach Ben Johnson loves to run the ball. And the former seventh-round pick has proven he can be a consistent force in the offense. Johnson undoubtedly wants Monangai back on the field as soon as possible. That reality is becoming increasingly likely as the Week 8 Seattle Seahawks clash looms. The Bears are set to release their first injury report of the week on Thursday. How Monangai is listed will be telling of his Week 8 status. But he seems more likely to suit up than he has in past weeks, via Jeremy Fowler of ESPN. “Bears running back Kyle Monangai (turf toe) has missed the past three weeks, but his chances are better of playing this week,” Fowler wrote. The injury bug has bitten the Bears heavily on both sides of the ball in 2026. They’ve managed to battle through, holding a 5-2 record heading into Monday Night Football. Still, Chicago is hoping to have a cleaner bill of health as the season progresses. In terms of Monangai, the franchise will continue to be cautious with his recovery. Still, the fact he wasn’t placed on injured reserve was a sign Chicago didn’t expect him to miss four or more games. away.headline: Ben Johnson provides injury rehab update on Bears S Coby Bryant
away.blurb: Bryant suffered a knee injury back in training camp that required surgery, and he was expected to miss four to six months, putting his estimated return around early December, which would be big as Chicago looks to make a playoff push down the stretch. Bears head coach Ben Johnson was asked about Bryant's progress, and he said the next month will tell the team a lot about his recovery and whether he can return. With the original 4-6 month timeline, Johnson said Bryant is "on track," but the next few weeks will be key. On the same day, Bryant also took to socials to discuss his rehab process, and it certainly sounds like he's gearing up for a return later this year. Bears Catch a Huge Break on Seahawks Week 8 Injury Report Skip to main content SI.COM While the Seattle Seahawks should soon be getting much healthier on offense, with running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returning to the lineup soon, they also received some bad news in the injury department on Monday. Offensive tackle Charles Cross has developed into a Pro Bowl-caliber player for Seattle. He has only allowed five pressures all season and has earned a 79.1 overall grade from Pro Football Focus (which ranks eighth among tackles). Unfortunately for Seattle, the Seahawks will be without Cross for their Week 8 matchup against the Bears on Monday night. According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz , the star left tackle suffered a high ankle sprain in the fourth quarter of the team's Sunday night clash against Kansas City. The Bears' pass-rush should have an opportunity to thrive on Monday night Specifically, Sweat should boost a defensive line that has performed far better than expectations through the first seven weeks of the season. Chicago is tied for seventh with 19 sacks thus far. The emergence of nickelback Kyler Gordon as a certifiable threat off the edge is a major reason for their pass-rushing success, but edge rusher Austin Booker has also played a key role. They're both tied for the team lead with four sacks. home.blurb: And first-round rookie Jadarian Price has been out with a chest injury for the past four games. With Charbonnet thought to be close to a return against Kansas City, the Seahawks opted for the safe approach, ramping up Zach after so much time out. In short, both are in the frame to return against the Bears. Price, on the other hand, hasn't missed as much time as Zach and has had a full offseason, so four weeks out isn't that big of a deal. Still, there may be a need to ease Price back into the picture, as you don't want two running backs returning from injury at the same time, likely with limited snaps.
